name: Mission Cantina
context: Time: night; Season: spring; Temperature: warm; Weather: partly cloudy
summary: Chef Danny Bowien offers modern Mexican food in a cool, colorful room that's a magnet for hipsters. Service options: Delivery; Popular for: Lunch, Dinner, Solo dining; Offerings: Alcohol, Beer, Cocktails, Comfort food, Hard liquor, Quick bite, Vegetarian options; Dining options: Lunch, Dinner; Amenities: Bar onsite; Atmosphere: Casual; Crowd: Locals; Payments: Debit cards Danny Bowien has been making quite a splash in the lower east side for the past year or two. From his Mission Chinese spot, which was shuttered due to rat infestation, to his newly minted Mexican joint Mission Cantina, which attempts to fuse traditional elements with hipster aesthetics. Bowien is an expert in bold flavors and when I say bold, I mean bold. Dare I say too bold, because sometimes his dishes mire the texture of the food from being appreciated due to how overly bombastic it is to your taste buds. That said, his dishes are always original and fun. Whether we're talking roasted beet tacos with jalapeno mole or his chili roasted lamb and crispy skate tacos, Bowien is not afraid of risks. Personal picks would be the spicy pickled veggies, the San Diego fries (think disco fries Mexican style) and the over the top peanuty chocolate chicken, which literally tastes like...chicken covered in chocolate with peanuts. The margaritas are a winner to, opting for a light agave mix instead of over sugary sour mix however I was less impressed with his horchata which was overpowered by too much espresso.  Bottom Line: If you're a fan of Bowien's outrageous style and/or Mission Chinese, Mission Cantina will be right up your alley, but don't be surprised if you leave with a nagging feeling that it should have been better.

name: Mercedes-Benz of Syracuse
context: Time: night; Season: autumn; Temperature: warm; Weather: heavy drizzle
summary: Service options: In-store shopping; Offerings: Oil change, Repair services; Payments: Checks, Debit cards, Credit cards My dissatisfaction with the overall buying experience. I will start with fact your salesman called me to make some changes to the deal that was prepared for me. I was hesitant at 1st (he wanted more money down, higher interest rate). After a few phone calls back and forth he told me that he needed to move some numbers around to make it work. That he was throwing in a maintenance package no charge to me plus giving me a little more on my trade in, so he could make it work. I questioned him a few times and he said correct I'm throwing it in.  On delivery of the car, the salesman had everything highlighted (where I needed to sign). It was nice because with me working 2 jobs I did not have a lot of time. He rushed my through filling out the paperwork which I appreciated. At the end I asked him what the maintenance package included? He told me the car will notify you but oil changes. Me not thinking anything of it because it was I was told it was free to me.  After driving the car that day I noticed a white residue on my black pants not sure where it came from. The next morning I notice a yellowing spot on the driver's seat that matched up with the spot on my dress pants. I decided to inspect the car more closely (including the paperwork). I thought with the referral I had and the car being certified pre owned by Mercedes Benz I could have trust in it but I was wrong. I found many more issues including the paperwork which the Salesperson lied to me about. I was charged for the Maintenance package it was a $2,030 line item. When I brought it to there attention they told me it came of the back end not the front end(have no clue what that means). Me being naive thinking maybe they took it off the trade in or sale price, I looked back at the 1st deal that was made and nothing changed. At this point I was very disappointed, me being a General Manager in the service industry for the last several years I could not fathom this. I chalked it up to the typical sly used cars tactics and to never do business there again which is sad because I buy a car every year or so.  The issues continued throughout the less than 1 year ownership of the car. Between mechanical and service issue with the car and dealership.  When I brought the car in for it's 1st maintenance service that was " included"  for $2,030 all that was done was and oil change, wiper blades, remote battery. So I paid $1,015 because it only came with 2 services for that price. Seemed crazy to me.  After about a year I decided to sell the car. Not only do the unhappiness with the car and dealership but because I never keep a car over a year. I tried getting a refund on the $1,015 on the pre paid maintenance which they told me they don't do that. And they asked why would I pre pay for 2 year maintenance if I was not going to keep it that long? When I was buying the car I told salesman numerous times that I would have the car paid off in a year looking to get something else. He was well aware I was not keeping the car longer than that.  I am writing this review a few weeks after selling the car because I did not want to have more hurdles at the dealership while I still hand ownership of it. There is a lot more I could say but hopefully this helps.

name: 1-800-PACK-RAT Moving and Storage
context: Time: night; Season: summer; Temperature: hot; Weather: hailstorm
summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance All around terrible experience, do not hire this company.  My client hired this company, pack rat moving and storage, to provide a pod for her relocation. She was moving from Tukwila to Bonney Lake, a straightforward move. On move day, they came to pick up the pod but told her it’s too heavy, she would have to remove items from the pod. It was just normal stuff in there, and they never told her about a weight limit. She was ready to unload it right then, but they would t wait. They told her they would be back at 11p that evening to pick it up. The buyers had possession at 6p, so that wasn’t good, but it was what they could do.  My client and I waited until 11p, they never showed up! To make matters worse, the pod was in the way of the buyers being able to move in. I called them the next day to find out what happened, and they said they didn’t know, but they would call me back ASAP and let me know when it would be picked up.  They never called me back, and another day went by. The buyers are irate at this point, threatening a lawsuit for damages because they can’t get into their property with the pod in the way. I called them again and spoke with a supervisor, who said it would take another 12 days for the pod to be picked up! At this point, my client hired a different moving company to unload the pod and take her stuff to her house, so the buyers would understand it wasn’t her fault.  I called again to let them know the pod is empty and they didn’t meet contract requirements, and they would need to refund my client. They said no, they wouldn’t refund because she used it for storage. Storage!?! Really!?! She hired them to move her stuff, and they utterly failed and got us into a mess with the buyers of her home.  Also, every time I called I waited on hold for at least 30 minutes. All around terrible experience.

name: Jeffrey's Appliance Service Inc
context: Time: evening; Season: winter; Temperature: cold; Weather: light freezing drizzle
summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance Our 1.25 year old GE Cafe refrigerator suddenly stopped cooling one day. We immediately called Jeffrey's and had them scheduled to come out the next day. The gentleman was on time, polite, super friendly and within 3 minutes had a good idea what the issue was. He explained to us that GE had issued a "service bulletin"months ago that certain GE refrigerators required a simple software update. He had no question that GE would cover his expenses for the service call and the software needed to fix the problem. He left us feeling optimistic that our very expensive fridge with an annoying software issue was going to be up and running again with no financial burden. We received a call the next day from Jeffrey's reporting that GE refused to cover the expenses because we were outside of our 1-year warranty by 4 months. The representative advised that we call GE ourselves as GE customers tend to hold more clout and may get an exception. I personally called GE explaining that we are VERY loyal GE customers currently owning more than 7 GE appliances. We had to toss hundreds of dollars of food out for a software glitch that we were never made aware of. I explained that it frustrated me that the "service bulletin" was released to repair facilities but not to the consumers and that it was released BEFORE our warranty had expired. GE made it very clear that they were not going to make an exception. So we accepted the fact that we were going to have to pay a couple of hundred dollars to have food in the house again. The good news?? Jeffrey's called us the next day and informed us that on their own, they called GE again on our behalf...without us asking them. Explaining again the issue that we were barely outside of our warranty and that this could have been avoided if we as the consumers were made aware of the required update. GE agreed to pay all expenses for the visit and the software that needed to be mailed and installed by a professional. This was not a HUGE expense that would have set us back greatly, but the fact that a large company like GE did so little to help and that Jeffrey's went to bat for us over principle was so admirable. We are beyond grateful for this service! Thank you!!!

context: Time: night; Season: autumn; Temperature: warm; Weather: rain shower
summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance Just moved our business to this area and first two orders shipped to us via USPS had issues: First package I got a notification from the seller of an issue with delivery; USPS tracking showed "Notice Left (No Authorized Recipient Available)", but we were there all day and so was our staff and there was no notice left.  Called the 800 number on that Wednesday and they informed us the local office indicates the re-attempt will happen on Saturday. I explained we are business that operates Mon-Fri.  I questioned why not deliver the next day?  I was instructed to call the local office.  NO ONE answers the phone, i tried for hours.  I started trying different numbers based on the number i was given (i.e. increment or decrement the last four digits of the number) and finally got the voice mail of a supervisor, who's outgoing message indicates to call the main local office number if there are questions about delivery and/or urgent issues.  I left my message with the supervisor and never got a call back.  Fortunately, the package was arrived the next day.  Second package; USPS tracking states "Undeliverable as Addressed".  Same vendor, same address, no difference. I called and called and called.  No one picks up the phone.  I left another message with supervisor.  given my first experience and what people have written on this site, i'm not hopeful, which has given me cause to write this review in hopes others do the same to help bring attention to changes needed to better serve our community.  I just don't understand how the local post offices provides the 800 number for customer service, but when you call the 800 number they tell you to call the local office.  There needs to be better national oversight and better collaboration.  That said, I believe this local office is not reflective of other local offices that are managed more efficiently.

name: Core Values Roadside Service LLC
context: Time: night; Season: summer; Temperature: hot; Weather: thunderstorm
summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance Before I get into the negative 99% of this review I want to give their driver Rick some credit. He seems to be the only honest person working for this company and the only one who knows what the hell customer service is. Thank you Rick (if you're reading this) for how polite and apologetic you were regarding the shortcomings of your office staff.  Now onto just about every other aspect of this company. Not once will I ever use them again. I have gone through multiple companies for roadside assistance and towing in the past and this has been the worst 21 hour process of getting my truck to the shop I have dealt with in my life.  I called my insurance (who I go through for roadside assistance) yesterday, July 11th at 5:35 pm saying that I would need my truck towed when I got home from work (at 7:30pm of the same day) due to it not running when I woke up for work yesterday. I explained to them that the time restraint was due to my friends shop closing at 8:30. My insurance called Core Values on my behalf to make the appointment 2 hours in advance of when I would need to be picked up. Core values told my insurance that the appointment was set and that they would be here at 7:30.  By 7:37 they had not shown up yet. I understand that a 7 minutes late is an understandable amount of time to be late to something like this, but I had not even gotten a confirmation call or a text from my insurance stating that the truck had been dispatched. I called my insurance who connected me to core values. The woman on the other line stated that they were running a little late but would be there in 30 minutes or less. An hour later they had still not shown up so I called my insurance to cancel the call.  Fast forward to today. I set up a tow again. No time constraints because it's my day off, I simply needed it towed. Request for assistance was officially accepted at 12:14 and core values said they would be there by 1:29pm. At 1:26 I get a call directly from core values, though they only let the phone ring once then hung up. I call them back. Younger woman on the phone this time and her tone sounded like she was pained to even touch a phone call. Never have I heard someone sound like they hated their job more than this girl. She transfers me to the older woman I was talking to the night before. This woman says that my tow will be later than expected but only 15-20 minutes. I say ok as the woman is talking over me then she hangs up.  1:44 I call my insurance again. I tell them this is the second time this has happened to me where they keep postponing my appointment. My insurance calls core values with me on the line. Lady from core values says the driver will be there in 12 minutes. Once she is off the line I express my concerns with my insurance. My insurance rep says to call them back if they do not arrive again within the stated time.  40 MINUTES LATER I still had not seen a truck. I call my insurance and tell them to cancel the call and just send a different company. As I am on the phone the driver finally arrives.  I have a text message stating they would be here at 1:29. The copy of the tow bill says an arrival time of 2:00. They actually showed up at 2:30. They not once told me an hour late. I informed my insurance of the 2 separate instances and they said they put in the complaint and would not be using Core values any longer.  Avoid this company at all costs.

name: Inspirations Ceramic & Art Cafe
context: Time: morning; Season: winter; Temperature: cold; Weather: snow
summary: From the business: Identifies as women-led; Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance My daughter and I attended one of the classes offered - one of their paint & sip classes. It was a lot of fun! The staff were very friendly and knowledgeable, and super helpful for a beginner such as myself. It was a relaxed evening, shared amongst a small room of strangers, who by the end of class seemed more like friends. I have social anxiety so group activities, especially with people I don't know, are very stressful to say the least. However, once I stepped foot inside the door, it was like coming home. They provide such a warm, inviting, safe, encouraging and artistic environment that I was able to enjoy my first night out in years - and make a pretty cool Seahawks mug in the process. What prevents me from a 5-star rating is that it can get a bit expensive pretty quick because you get sweet up in picking out the perfect piece you want to paint, and some pieces cost much more than others. I would still definitely go back, and plan to in the future, especially since I know to be extra careful about pricing when picking out the item(s) to paint. I don't believe that they are misrepresenting anything or being sneaky about pricing because this is a very upstanding, professional and caring businesses. You just need to make sure and ask questions when picking out what you want to paint so there won't be any surprises. Ahhhhh heck, I'm going to up my review to 5-stars because the pricing issue could very well be chalked up to my first time being out and doing something new in a very long time. It's not their fault I have anxiety, and they were very interested in making me feel comfortable. Give this place a try, you won't regret it!

summary: Italian restaurant serving steak & classic entrees in a modest space with patio seating. Service options: Delivery It was ok, we went for mothers day, at 1 pm.  They were not too friendly, but not unfriendly.  The waitress seemed afraid of the situation. We were a larger party, 11 of us all together.  The food was what you would expect for the money, it filled the belly but didn't really make an impression.  The atmosphere was sterile.  It was obvious that the salad plates were very old, they were all scratched up.  All in all, the food wasn't bad, simple American Italian with the classic red pepper flake and parmesan shakers at the ready.  I ordered the veal parmesan.  It was cooked ok, about what you would expect, it came with a side of penne pasta.  The sauce was barely mediocre but for the price it was fine.  I had asked for coffee, and found it to be acceptable.  My only real complaint was that the refills had to be requested and I waited about 20 minutes before i figured that out.  I certainly wouldn't avoid this place, but I'm not planning any dates with my honey here.  I would not classify this atmosphere as date worthy, which is a shame, because for very little money they could put a much warmer atmosphere together.  A bit more confidence and attentiveness from the server would go a long way and some darker paint on the walls could give an illusion of romance.  If you are looking for a place to fill your belly that's reasonably priced, you won't be disappointed.  If you are looking for a dinner date spot, you would be better off at Applebee's or most any other budget style chain restaurant.  Don't expect the best of service, but it will be adequate.

name: Bellingham Fitness
context: Time: night; Season: winter; Temperature: warm; Weather: drizzle
summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance This review is based solely on price. The trial period is a week. So when I bring up contract later, remember you only get a week.  I have been bullied, and taken advantage of by gyms in the past. Anyone can say "that shouldn't happen" but it doesn't change the fact that it did, and it left a mark. So there was a few things I wanted to check.  Lets start by saying that pricing on their website is misleading. If you want to pay $15 every 2 weeks, then you have to be part of a 24 month contract. If you want 12 months you have to pay $100 upfront. If you don't want to be locked in to a contract and run the risk of history repeating itself, then you have to pay $200 upfront. The only way you can get out of said contracts is if you move, or are injured. Still have to bring them proof though.  So lets give an example of why I'm saying this. As someone with severe depression and anxiety. Someone who has a hard enough time leaving their own home. If something happens where I don't want to go there anymore, where its SO bad that I just want to write them off and never go back? TOO BAD! They'll still charge you. You're in a contract. Thats how they get you.  These things might be ok to people who already work out that often, but to anyone who is unsure or who has had bad experiences in the past it comes off as more of a scam than anything else. Just another place that only cares about money. Sad, but experience dictates that thats the only thing these places are for. Making people believe they're there to help, when really its just about the wallet.  Enjoy your time at the gym.

context: Time: afternoon; Season: summer; Temperature: hot; Weather: heavy rain
summary: Service options: Takeout, Dine-in; Health & safety: Staff required to disinfect surfaces between visits; Popular for: Lunch, Dinner; Offerings: Comfort food, Quick bite; Amenities: Good for kids; Atmosphere: Casual I'm not even sure where to start with this place. I can't believe it has been like 11 years since this business started. I remember finding the modest, but oh so worth it, little pizza joint on fruitvale. Me loving pizza like I do, of course had to check this place out and boy was I impressed! Let's start out with it being a local business and not just that,  but own by one of the nicest couples in town that I've come in contact with at their business. They have this way of making you feel like an important customer, scratch that, friend, when you call in and also when you see them. Throw in some arcade'age while you wait and it's no wonder why this is my absolute top rated pizza place in Yakima since the day I first stepped foot into there. It's a brick oven type of pizza with amazing sauce, fresh ingredients and all the love that really makes these pizzas not even in the same ballpark as other big chain branches. Mr. Pizza is in a league of it's own. The only thing that I so wish they still had, literally one of the saddest things to ever let go of, was the sweet potato pizza. Oh......My.......Gosh! The first time I read that I was like ehh I don't know about that, fast forward 1,850 sweet potato pizzas later, maybe not that exact number, but you get the point, and I would give up any other kind of pizza forever just to eat that one for the rest of my life. It seriously was that good. Maybe with enough effort we could rally and convince them to bring it back! 😏 😉  Back to the review.....so whether you're wanting to try a new pizza place, want a quick pizza made with friendly workers or you just want to go enjoy the amazing smells, Mr. Pizza is my absolute #1 pick and I don't believe that will ever change.

context: Time: morning; Season: summer; Temperature: warm; Weather: thunderstorm
summary: Family-friendly eatery & bar known for a wide American comfort-food menu & Western-themed environs. Service options: Delivery, Dine-in; Highlights: Great dessert; Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance, Wheelchair accessible parking lot, Wheelchair accessible seating; Offerings: Alcohol, Coffee, Comfort food, Healthy options; Dining options: Lunch, Dinner; Amenities: Bar onsite; Atmosphere: Casual; Crowd: Groups; Planning: Accepts reservations The only reason I am not giving this Claim Jumper the lowest possible rating is because I have to have a way to distinguish the lowest of the low, like Golden Chopstick's was in my experience.  Claim Jumper is not quite that bad.  I went there Friday to get a carry out order for my wife.  I ordered the lemon pepper zucchini spears with extra parmesan and the ranch dressing in a different bag so it wouldn't chill the zucchini.  As I later learned the person taking the order entered it incorrectly.  When my wife opened the container she found that instead of extra parmesan there was none at all.  I called and spoke to Isis and she was courteous but only offered to replace the order - my name would be in the "VIP book" and a manager would speak with me when I came back.  My issue with that is even if I'm dining in an incorrect order costs me time (money) and satisfaction (more than money.)  For a carry out order it also costs more time and the price of traveling (gas, wear on the car and frustration.)  If you screw up my order and want my business you need to do more than "make it a little better", you need to "make it right".  For special occasions I spend significant sums at reliable restaurants, if that is what it takes for an establishment to care.  I previously spent a large sum there on my anniversary - telling them it was my anniversary - and they screwed it up so badly I didn't go back for over a year.  Mollified if not exactly satisfied I went back tonight, Monday evening.  Instead of having the incident recorded (as far as I could tell from my interaction) I got to tell the manager on duty, Alex, the whole thing again.  He seemed a bit hard of listening but offered to replace the order, in a less pleasing manner than Isis had.  More time and satisfaction wasted.  When the replacement was delivered and I got it home my wife found that the parmesan on it was minimal (Alex had given me extra parmesan on the side which I accepted in puzzlement, not being sure how to handle it in the moment), the zucchini was undercooked such that the breading didn't want to stay attached.  (It did have the lemon pepper on it this time, which made it obvious it had not been there the previous time.)  My history with this Claim Jumper location is that they can get my order right less than half the time, when they get it wrong my experience of getting it fixed is barely even "almost good enough" less than half the time and I am just deeply unsatisfied with them.  They need to learn to manage their quality control, internal communication and customer service much better if they want to stay in business.

I told them I could hear them and she was quick to tell me that she basically did care that I was standing there listening to her bash me. Feeling angry and offended I took my check and walked out. I will never go there again for parts or services ever, they for sure lost me as a customer!!!

Only change in my rating would be to give Rite Aid a ZERO, but this service won't allow that!

name: United States Postal Service
context: Time: morning; Season: autumn; Temperature: cold; Weather: light drizzle
summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance I recently moved.  I told the post office, and they have been dutifully putting new address stickers on my mail and I have been getting them.  I ordered something from Amazon.  I made one mistake: I updated my billing address but not my shipping address.  When I discovered my error, it was too late, the package had been shipped.  The USPS has a tracking system.  Whenever a package goes through a point in the USPS, a scanner scans it and makes a note of where and when the package was seen.  I followed the package to a major post office in Kent, WA.  Then it arrived at my old post office in a few hours.  Then delivery was interrupted.  Then the package arrived at the Bitter Lake post office at 5:21 in the morning October 30th.  October 31st, I called them.  They said the package had been delivered.  It had not.  They said the carrier distinctly remembered delivering a package to my house.  I described the package to them, and they admitted that that was not the package he delivered.  They said they would look for it. I called on November 1st.  They said that they hadn't found it.  It must have been returned to Amazon.  I asked them why it hadn't been scanned when it left.  They said they had been busy.  I pointed out to them that since return to sender was very unusual, the customer probably would want to know that.  You do stamp those things return to sender, don't you?  He said that it may have gone back to the original post office.  So I called them, and they said that would not happen, it would go back to the same post office in Kent that the package came from originally.  So I called the Bitter Lake post office again, and they assured me that the package had been returned to the sender.  I asked them if that was unusual because you've been delivering my other mail.  Saturday afternoon, I got an E-mail message from the USPS that package had been delivered to the front door of my house.  I came home, and sure enough, it had.  What really angers me more than anything else is the advertising they played while I was on hold.  "You can depend on the post office to get your packages delivered".  Unfortunately, since I live where I live, I am stuck with this post office.

context: Time: morning; Season: spring; Temperature: warm; Weather: partly cloudy
summary: Self-serve seafood eatery with waterfront views. Service options: Curbside pickup, Takeout, Dine-in, Delivery; Popular for: Lunch, Dinner, Solo dining; Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance; Offerings: Beer, Coffee, Comfort food, Healthy options, Vegetarian options, Wine; Dining options: Lunch, Dinner, Catering, Dessert; Amenities: Good for kids, High chairs, Wi-Fi; Atmosphere: Casual, Cozy, Romantic, Upscale; Crowd: Groups, Tourists; Payments: Debit cards, Credit cards ***DISCLAIMER: rating not representative of the very good food quality👍 but of the disappointing😦 service we received***  Duryea's Lobster Deck has an original ordering concept that you can usually only find in all-you-can-eat sushi restaurants. After being sit, you're handed the menu and an ordering sheet📝 where you can circle the items and quantities you want to order. Then, you get up to hand it to the counter and pay💵 right away. Good thing, the menu prices are with 🎊Service included🎉.  This kinda gives a convivial atmosphere than is emphasized by the picnic looking tables. You even get blankets when it's cold or windy!  We ordered the baked and raw clams which both were excellent. So were the oysters. Very good food.  I found it very pricey but, it's the Hamptons and Montauk, you know the 💸drill💸.  ----------------------------------------  So why only the two stars, when it obviously deserved four!? We also ordered Clam Chowder. We didn't get Clam Chowder but Lobster Bisque. (they are really easy to differentiate, the former is a broth with Clam chunks when the latter is thick and creamy without chucks). So we informed the waiter which, after checking with the kitchen, ensured us it was Clam Chowder. Then comes the manager insisting it's Clam Chowder and that they have changed the recipe. You can make mistakes, we may even had keep it. But lying to you customers is not ok. Plus, we French take our food seriously, and aren't easy to fool!  ----------------------------------------  So should you go? Definitely if you're ok with the prices. Just ask for the recipe first if you're into Clam Chowder..

summary: Snug, low-lit sushi house providing a wide variety of rolls & Japanese plates in a low-key ambiance. I explained that my best friend was picking up the food instead of me, as I wasn't near and she was on her way to me. I was told no, and that since the food was already made I wasn't allowed to cancel my order. I explained the circomstances to no avail.  They expected me to drive 45 mins from Lockport NY to Buffalo because of thier no paying over the phone policy, when my best friend lives near Delaware Park. It was a Thursday, and I had already driven 45mins to and from my office in downtown Buffalo. I was put on a "no serve list" simply because my best friend, to no fault of her own, was having an awefull week financially. I discovered I was on this list when I ordered lunch for my entire office, I used my phone to make the order, completely unaware of this list. I had a nice conversation with the lady that took the call, I made the order and was told 20mins. I drove the 10mins from my office to Wasabi, with my phone, & I hadn't missed a single phone call, I checked! I sat in the car and waited 10mins, so I wasn't hovering in the rather small dinning area Wasabi has, then go in to be told that my 5 meal order was not made, and would not be made as I am on a "no serve list." The meal was about $50 I had $100 cash with me, I explained that this was for my entire office, not just me, that 4 other people would be effected by this policy. They refused, absolutely refused, to even consider making my coworker's and Boss' meal, even with me offering to pay them double the order in cash! Now, I hate it when people make a scene, I absolutely do! But simply because I am not the loud type doesn't mean I wasn't or am not upset! So I left quietly, but I want to make it clear that I am having my family attorney review the legality of the no pay over the phone policy, and it's subsequent no serve policy, as both feel rather discriminatory, and disparaging against the less fortunate among us. Imagine if I had been a mom of an out of state student, who was starving and needed food but just didn't have the money? If this policy stays in place, a child could posibly starve to death. I understand that there are other restaurants in the world. But could you imagine if they all had this poorly thought out policy?  Now I do want to be fair and honest in my review! So I do have to say that other that this awefull experience, the service at Wasabi had been phenominal. And the food, I assume, is still great. But as you can see, this policy is overshadowing, and has the potential to continue to overshadow, the fantastic work you guys are and have been doing.

name: Equinox Apartments
context: Time: night; Season: winter; Temperature: cold; Weather: snow
summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance, Wheelchair accessible parking lot So much. There are arbitrary, harsh policies invented and enforced suddenly. Around Christmas, they started sending packages back that weren't picked up immediately. Recently, they started a $45 fine per box left unbroken-down, and when I asked about it, I was rudely accused of looking for loopholes. They now charge a fortune for friends/family to park in the garage, and immediately tow unauthorized vehicles parked in their outside parking (instead of leaving a note and waiting 24 hours like they used to). There's a $50 "convenience fee" if you pay rent using a card, on top of the credit card fee, which you also pay. They also raise rates constantly, like pet-rent and the price of monthly parking (because they heard someone nearby was charging more). Cars are still broken into about every 6 months, including mine. I'm sick of having to deal with changes that affect me without being able to voice an opinion or move out.  I almost always have to go in multiple times to get anything done, which, as a non-confrontational person, is really difficult. There have been issues that took them months to resolve. For instance, my balcony decoration was blown onto a ledge, which I asked the building to retrieve. It took a few days (they needed permission before going through a vacant apartment), but they left it outside "to dry," and the decoration must have been blown away again. I went in every week to ask about it, it was expensive and I loved it, and they passed blame around from maintenance to cleaning to people I've never heard of, claiming they had it somewhere and they just couldn't find it, but that it was damaged anyway *hint hint*. I'd seen it from my balcony, and no, it wasn't. After 2 months I asked if they could just reimburse me, and they said no. Once the water didn't get hot for more than a month, apparently for all apartments, and keys, electronic or not, can't just be traded in when they stop working, it takes time, during which you're SOL. I've asked a hundred times for a broom for the yoga room, and we still don't have one.  The hallway walls are covered in grease and dents, and the floors are stained and smelly. The stairwells were absolutely disgusting. I had to let them know about a bag of dog poo, and a bunch of recycling left there, neither was taken care of quickly. After 3 trips in to ask about it, they finally *just* had them cleaned. The recycling/garbage room has no ventilation, is tiny, gross, and a pain to get to, but it has a nice camera, to watch residents. There are tons of things that don't work, never have, and probably never will, like the electric fire pit in the courtyard, or the close-button in the elevator, which btw, is 'down' AT LEAST once a week for maintenance, moving, or because it's broken again. The fire alarms go off constantly. Since I moved in, it's gone off for legitimate reason once; it was freezing, the crowd was 15 people, and a bunch of them snuck back in before the fire department even got here. They have mistakes and "test alarms" which means they go for hours, off-and-on, in our homes and hallways. It terrifies our pets and children, makes it difficult to work, and it's dangerous and irresponsible to not be taken seriously. When I finally sent an email to complain, they said they sent it to the manager, who would get back to me, and she didn't. Also, he maintenance guy isn't treated very well by the building.  A third of my view is great (despite power lines), the rest is a filthy roof and the homeless camp under the interstate, and we pay over $3,000 a month (two bedroom) for it. Many of the apartments aren't rented to people, but to businesses (Adoba, Amazon, etc); I think it's part of why rent is so high. No one seems to live here very long. Lastly, I'm sick of getting blown-off and screwed by someone else's mistakes. When their auto-payment system broke, I had to pay late fees. When they realized my boyfriend hadn't been charged enough for parking, they made him pay the difference, in-full and immediately. I have 100 more complaints, but I'm out of characters.

ItsI also true that you share a washe heater, so, be sure you don't want a shower if you have neighbors who also do. As the Astoria location was closed, we drove all the way to the Glen Cove one. The place looked like it didn't belong in New York, but in Miami with trees and dim lit lights. The interior has a modern vibe, with decorative pictures, and bright recess lights. The staff were very helpful and hospitable. We ordered for takeout as they were closing up, but they still gave us green tea and firnee (dessert on the house) while we waited for our food.  The food was delicious! However, the portions were small. The uzbeki palaw comes with carrots only. I was anticipating both carrots and raisins but perhaps some places don't include raisins. The lamb chops entree comes with 4 pieces of lamb chops. I'd recommend the combo platter to get a taste of all meats! The sauces were ample and tasted great.  The firnee and shir birinj were delicious as well. They were nice and soft--neither hard nor overly sweet. It was perfect!  They also had some bottled white sauce for sale ($5 a bottle). If you want some extra white sauce to go, you know what to do!

Free on first Thursdays and well worth the admission on other days.  Step into the museum and explore the rich history of Asian Americans in the US and in Seattle. Take the tour and walk through a hotel from the 1890, seeing what it was like to be an Asian immigrants at a time when they had to live in hotels, because it was illegal to own homes. Great for families and individuals.

context: Time: evening; Season: winter; Temperature: cold; Weather: clear
summary: Service options: In-store shopping The only reason this dealership gets 2 stars is because of the buying process. After purchasing a Ford f-150 from this small dealership (a husband and wife) which was a pleasant experience, I had a check engine light come on within the first week for lean bank one and two. I brought it in and they told me my oil cap was loose and reset the code. Within a week the light came back on with the same code. This time they had it all day and told me "you must be using bad gas or running it too low. It was at a ¼ tank which meant there was still 5 gallons left in it. Obviously they didn't do anything more than clear the code, because I brought it to my regular shop and they scanned it and told me it's a p2006 code which means the  Intake Manifold Runner Control Is Stuck Closed. Now I'm looking at $400.00 minimum to have this issue fixed, and I've only had it a month and a half and only put 1000 miles on it. Its NOT a loose oil cap, its NOT bad gas, it IS however a mechanic that doesn't want to service a vehicle correctly. Another issue was which I forgot to mention to them originally was a vibration com from the front end. I replaced the stock wheels with aftermarket wheels and tires and still had the same issue. I jacked up the front and could feel a side to side wiggle,which means bad tie rods. I personally replaced them... No More Vibrations. I mentioned it to his wife and she said it was the aftermarket wheels which I had on a different truck, EVEN AFTER I told her I replaced the tie rod ends As they say buyer beware.

context: Time: evening; Season: winter; Temperature: warm; Weather: mostly clear
summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance Rude, unhelpful, and confusing. Friday the week before I asked someone if I could ship a non-standard package (doesn't fit in an express box) if I could ship, this was at 15 minutes to closing and I was getting a quote for someone. They gave me a quote and rushed me out the door without explaining the details on package preparation or anything. This contrasts with both UPS and FedEx which both gave me quotes, and information on shipping, and will assist you with packing and give you all information up front.  This morning I go in with the information given to me, they were curt, unhelpful, and interrupted me while I was attempting to explain my situation. Normally I do not ship with USPS and was unfamiliar with the system, this was a request for a client.  I can't tell if they were angry because I was asking for service while they were receiving greeting cards, or if the 2 other people in line, or because I had my phone out with the address to send the package to.  I have had better experiences elsewhere in the past, this is definitely an anomaly.

Everyone was great, the ambience was lovely, the food was 98% fresh, but the "special roll" in the middle of the course pandered to American tastes. It nearly ruined the whole meal, but the fantastic additional sashimi course that I ordered was still too fresh in my mind for me to feel too bad. The "special roll" was very beautiful: a piece of art. I should have just looked at it and not put it in my mouth. The caviar carefully placed on each slice was too tempting, so I took a piece to try. It was a mediocre shrimp tempura wrapped in seaweed, wrapped in rice, topped with white fish, topped with plentiful sticky sweet brown sauce, topped with caviar (perhaps topped with sansho?). It was a monument to American taste, with a hint of Japan. Okay okay, but this is how much it distracted from the rest of the VERY good meal... After this came the 7 pieces of chef's choice sushi. Yum! I didn't care for the shrimp (cooked shrimp on rice always makes me feel like I'm sitting at the kids table), but every other nigiri was divine. I actually struggled to figure out what order to eat them in... When it came time for dessert I couldn't bear to look at it after that sweet shrimp roll from earlier, so  took it to go. We also had the daiginjo Konteki, which was very nice. All in all not a bad experience, but I very much regret ordering the course, and it is all just a bit overpriced. Order your items one by one and avoid anything with dragon in the name! Happy eating to you!

name: Hermann J. Wiemer Vineyard
context: Time: night; Season: autumn; Temperature: cold; Weather: fog
summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance What can I say?  This is THE place for wine on the Finger Lakes; it is the gold standard and the Holy Grail.  Any serious wine aficionado needs to make a stop here.  Their Rieslings are top-notch, as good or better than any others in the area and comparable with the German and Austrian wines that so many wineries on the Finger Lakes seek to emulate.  They do other whites with style as well (including a fine Gewurztraminer) and they make sweet wines with the same attention to quality as their dry offerings.  Their sparkling wines are also worthwhile (with the only slight flaw being a less-than-fantastic Sekt-style sparkling Riesling).  Make an appointment for a tasting and spend some serious time here, then buy a good quantity of their wine.  Their prices are mostly quite reasonable (especially for the quality) and the tasting staff know their stuff.  They have been making splendid wines since at least the mid-nineties and just seem to keep getting better.  They deserve six stars.

name: Ballinger Chevron
context: Time: evening; Season: spring; Temperature: warm; Weather: mostly clear
summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance This review is for Ballinger Towing.  Everything seemed to be going well. Adam was helpful on the phone. I did think that since I had a flexible pick up time, and was willing to work on the scheduling of this tow for multiple vehicles, that the price was a little high but I was willing to do it to support a neighborhood business.  Lots of communication throughout the day had me feeling pretty confident.  I had requested service after midnight (but anytime before 6am) on either Thursday or Friday, and we had agreed on midnight Thursday. So, at 9pm when I received the text message saying that they were ready in the next hour, I explained, "No, we said AFTER midnight, remember?".  Ok, was the last message and contact I ever got.  No response to repeated texts and calls throughout the night.  When he did finally answer my call this morning (after I blocked my number), and inquired what had happened to our scheduled appointment last night, Adam responded,  "I was wondering the same thing..."  "Well, Adam, no calls and no texts from you and my cars are still in the same location. I never heard from you last night. I was hoping for an explanation or apology."  I was surprised and disappointed when he rudely and abruptly said, "This conversation is over."  Now, thankfully I wasn't standing, in distress on the side of the road with a flat tire or disabled automobile.  But, I was very flexible, offered to work with them so that they could in the local area rather than have to cross to the opposite part of town and this is how I am repaid.  A good town truck driver is something that I use with regularity since I am in the transportation industry and routinely buy vehicles. I just looked it up and saw that I towed 8 vehicles last year. I will never use this company nor refer others to them.

name: Starbucks
context: Time: morning; Season: spring; Temperature: warm; Weather: mostly clear
summary: Seattle-based coffeehouse chain known for its signature roasts, light bites and WiFi availability. Service options: Delivery, Takeout, Dine-in; Highlights: Fast service, Great coffee, Great dessert, Great tea selection; Popular for: Breakfast, Lunch, Solo dining, Good for working on laptop; Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance, Wheelchair accessible restroom; Offerings: Coffee, Prepared foods, Quick bite; Dining options: Breakfast, Dessert; Amenities: Good for kids, Restroom, Wi-Fi; Atmosphere: Casual, Cozy; Crowd: College students, Tourists; Planning: Usually a wait; Payments: Debit cards, NFC mobile payments I have some deep feelings about this Starbucks location. Not because I love Starbucks, but because there are changes afoot in this neighborhood and this place is a metaphor for many of them.  Let's start with the fact that it exists here a all. Whenever a Starbucks comes to a neighborhood in NYC it's a sign not of impending gentrification, but of solidly underway gentrification. Starbucks is not showing up in the hopes that gentrified folks are around, and looking at the people who live mostly on the west side of Broadway? It's clear: the gentrifiers have succeeded.  This Starbucks also here because other cafes have paved the way. In the last 10 years we went from having no cafes to having a burst of a ton of cafes to having fewer cafes because many of them didn't make it. Why? There are a lot of reasons, but the biggest is because it's an expensive business. You have to balance a lot of things. And you need a clientele willing to pay certain prices to keep you afloat.  Even in a gentrified nabe like this one there are still a ton of people who are concerned with authenticity and local-ness (as long as those things are made to feel comfortable and welcoming to THEM and not necessarily the people who lived around here before them). So I can see them eschewing the Starbucks in favor of Darling Coffee down the road. Those people can keep that place.  After having spent several days in this Starbucks writing, working, and people watching, here's what I've noticed about it: a true mix of people comes in here. Yes, you have the white folks, the hipsters, the yuppies, and the baby carriage pushers. Those aren't the only people who come in. There are plenty people of color, especially Dominicans, who drop in for coffee or stay to work or hang out. This place is pretty hoppin' on weekend afternoons and on some weeknights. The people who work here are mostly brown, and as a brown person I appreciate that. Contrast this with the very white clientele and staff of Darling Coffee or even Taszo down in Wa-Hai.  Curious, that. A chain coffee shop draws a more diverse clientele than the "local" shops not so far away? How is that possible?  Maybe because Starbucks isn't only here for the gentrifiers. Maybe because the people of Inwood are a bit tired of "local" places that aren't so friendly toward what we consider local people.  One of the biggest drawbacks to this place is how few seats there are. A communal table in the center seats 6, bar seating by the window seats maybe 4, tables in the back corner can fit up to 8 if everyone is willing to get snug. I usually find a seat, even if I have to wait for a bit. It's worth it.  There are outlets, there is free wi-fi, there are good drinks (chai latte, come to mama), there are friendly people. I would spend all my days here before I spent an hour in certain other cafes.  I wish that they'd gone for a bigger space with this location. I wish that the other cafes in this neighborhood hadn't disappeared or made themselves unfriendly toward certain people. I wish we didn't need chain cafes to make other places step up their game. I wish hipsters and yuppies hadn't discovered Inwood. I wish a lot of things.

summary: Drugstore & pharmacy chain selling products including cosmetics, vitamins & mini-mart basics. Service options: Curbside pickup, Delivery, In-store pickup, In-store shopping, Same-day delivery; Health & safety: Mask required, Staff wear masks, Staff get temperature checks, Safety dividers at checkout; Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible elevator, Wheelchair accessible entrance; Planning: Quick visit; Payments: Checks, Debit cards, NFC mobile payments, Credit cards I live extremely close by and have tolerated this pharmacy for half a year, but no more. I have so many frustrating anecdotes that I don’t know which to share. - Frequent 15+ minute lines - I went to get a flu shot and stood in line for 10+ minutes. I was told to wait in a chair, and did so for another 5-10 minutes. Someone then came over and asked what I was waiting on, and I said a flu shot. Only then was I told that the person doing flu shots wasn’t there. - I went to pick up a prescription they’d alerted me was ready. I got there and it wasn’t ready. I waited off to the side. The line was clearly 15 min long and I wasn’t going to wait in it again. No one ever said anything to me. Eventually I had to cut the line and told them I was leaving for the airport in an hour for an international vacation (100% true), and they begrudgingly gave me my medication. The general case of “my medication wasn’t ready on time” is pretty common. Or if I’d need 2 meds, they’d only have one ready, so I’d have to either wait 15+ min or come back multiple times. - They autofilled a script I didn’t need automatically refilled. When I asked them to remove it from autofill, they canceled auto refill for ALL my prescriptions. - Duane Reade text alerts don’t tell you what medication is ready. This is enormously frustrating if you need multiple prescriptions. They cite HIPAA, but CVS lists the first 3 letters of a script and it’s so helpful.  This review is long enough, but rest assured, I could go on for quite a while.

name: Staples
context: Time: evening; Season: autumn; Temperature: warm; Weather: heavy drizzle
summary: Chain retailer offering brand-name electronics & print services, plus office supplies & furniture. Service options: Curbside pickup; Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance; Payments: Cash-only Earlier this year, on the 3rd of February, I purchased my first Staples 8-sheet Cross-cut Shredder for $49.99 on sale along with the SquareTrade Protection 2-year Standard Plan for an extra $9.99 at this Staples store. But last month, when I stopped by the Chase Bank across from it, I've noticed that it was empty. Perhaps it's been under construction or relocation. When it comes to electronics, I always feel the urge to get the extra manufacturer and store warranties as I think something is going to happen them and I'll need to repair or replace them which sometimes happens. So, that's the reason I added the the 2-year protection plan in my order. A store staff informed me that the smaller shredders don't last very long and were prone to become defective.  So far, it's been alright but I stopped using my shredder for a few months because I shredded too many envelopes with the clear plastic windows. After sitting in the living room for a while, I decided to open the top part of the shredder by taking it apart with a screwdriver. I discovered that large pieces of papers along with plastic sheets stuck in-between the cross-cut blades. And I was able to clear the paper jams and put it back together.  Lately, I've been shredding papers only and cautiously, but it also becomes overheated at which point I turned it off and turn it on only when I'm using it. I've shredded a few debit/credit cards and other plastic cards with ease. Accidentally, I did insert a few papers with staples still attached to them and my shredder handled them with ease.  Truthfully, if you're planning to buy a shredder for home or personal use, a 14-sheet cross-cut shredder with higher shredding cut capacity would be best for you. I've been shop comparison shredders on Amazon, Wal-Mart, Staples and Costco for 16-sheet to 30-sheet cross-cut, strip-cut and micro-cut shredders as I have the need to shred "lots of my old mailing envelopes from my previous addresses. LOL  I know what some of you maybe thinking, but it's a little hard to let go of some and certain things. And this is the reason I started with this little shredder. I do not recommend this shredder for heavy duty use at home or the office. Here are a few examples of the ones I'm considering :  - AmazonBasics 24-Sheet Cross-Cut Paper, CD, and Credit Card Shredder with Pullout Basket for $156.99 from Amazon,  - Staples 100-Sheet Auto-Feed Micro-Cut Shredder for $169.99 from Staples,  - Aurora JamFree AU1400XA 14-Sheet Cross-Cut Paper/CD/Credit Card Shredder with Pull-Out Wastebasket for $158.50 from Wal-Mart,  Consider a shredder that can handle CD, DVD, credit/debit cards, paper clips, staples and shred multiple sheet/papers at the same time silently or at low noise level as possible. I hope this review was helpful  towards purchasing your own shredders.

summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance Moved into this place right when they finished construction. Live there for a year. I wrote an honest review before but it magically disappeared, I believe owner or staff are going out of  their way to remove legitimate less then stellar reviews that are posted.  The view is gorgeous but that is about it.  A tiny 2 bedroom apartment with a water view when I moved in was $2,000. Which is on the higher end but I get it its a new building so they have to pay for the construction some how right. There are not any true amenities except for a gym which is a separate business. I think you only get one gym membership per household. It is not open from the lobby you have to enter on the outside. No classes just gym equipment and a room you can play workout videos in. There is no pool or hot tub, which would be nice. Most apartment places at least have a pool.  When I lived there. There was absolutely nothing else but the apartments. You would think it would make sense to at least build a grocery store or restaurant first  but after I moved thats when they added Two Town Pub.  The fire alarms constantly went off at 2-3am in the morning. EVERYONE in the building would come down outside and wait outside in the cold while the fire department came and fixed the system.  I had a crane outside of my window which didnt bug me too much but if you are off or at home they do construction 6 days a week including Saturday so expect to hear a lot of work being done...which will continue for years. It is moving along very very slowly.  The front desk women there are snarky and rude. They dont attempt to deliver packages and allow them to sit in the office until you go looking for the package. They will charge you small misc. fees here and there and its a good idea to monitor you account.  Move elsewhere. For the price and what you get its not worth it. You could find much nicer. I can only imagine how much they have increased the price of  living there since I moved. Im sure its ridiculous.

name: Mario Cuomo Bridge Pathway
context: Time: night; Season: summer; Temperature: hot; Weather: clear
summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance; Amenities: Good for kids Recently heard of the opening of the path. I saw it under construction for the last few months. I decided to make a trip on a quiet Monday afternoon. I intended to visit the Nyack (North) area but had some issues getting there. I was on 87 North and got off at exit 11 as the signs instructed, but after that it was a pain following the signs. I could not find the parking lot, but only a viewing area. There was a separate smaller entrance  from a side street, but I was unsure of the street parking regulations in the residential neighborhood so I passed on that. I got back on the 87 South and decided to go to the Tarrytown (South) parking location. After exiting off exit 9 the Path's parking lot was only a few minute ahead along the main road. (It was hard to miss) Parking was free and plentiful. They do require masks now and adequate signage directing so. There are bathrooms and vending machines as well as a coffee stand and "bike rental?" stand there as well. The scenery, as you can imagine, is gorgeous. There are stop areas along the path with seating areas. To all my fellows photographers out there...know that there is either glass or wire throughout the entire path...so unless you bring a zoom lens to zoom in between the wires, you won't get any clean shots. The path itself, like many have mentioned, is narrow. Especially when you consider there is about a 5 foot space for two-way walking/running and another space about the same size for two-way biking. Its hard to believe that cyclists would pass by each other and stay within that small area. On that day, it was not crowded, but I can imagine when the weather cools down and on weekend, you will notice a lot more people. Everyone was wearing masks. Overall I had a great time there. I would love to return with the family once the weather cools down. Come prepared and be realistic though... at 3.6 miles each way you may want to bring a snack or drink. You may also want to choose a cool and comfortable day. Also, be mindful of bringing younger children...you may end up carrying them on the walk back. :)

context: Time: night; Season: winter; Temperature: cold; Weather: snow
summary: Service options: In-store shopping; Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance; Offerings: Oil change, Repair services; Payments: Checks, Debit cards, Credit cards We have primarily had Kia automobiles (4) since 2011 and have been very happy with them all. When looking to replace our second car, a 2011 Kia Soul we were inclined to get another one. We wanted to check out the new 500X ( Lounge / Trekking ) model because we liked the style and features.  The sales people I dealt with were very nice, professional, and while motivated they were not pushy which was a pleasant surprise. That coupled with a good deal on a 2016 500X Lounge (identical to the one pictured here ) and the extras offered by the VIP plan made the switch more inviting.  Unfortunately while the 500X is a very good looking car it does not have the guts to back up its looks. The 9 speed automatic transmission ( we have read has been recalled about a half million times ) is a dog. It provides the car with virtually ZERO performance, and trying to pass or merge on a highway is dangerous (unless every car was a Prius ). The  side mirrors shake, the rear hatch creaks which is signs of shoddy build quality, the rear back up camera is useless at night with a dark, grainy picture and the driver power seat stopped working around 9000 miles. This car thankfully will go back in the fall of 2019, UNDER mileage because I hate driving it and only do so to keep the mileage down on my other lease. I will likely never get another Fiat again and I recommend you don't either. The Alfa's look nice and they are fast but very high priced and based on the fact they are made by the same company I would imagine a higher priced problem waiting to happen. I asked early on to turn the car in but they would not oblige so I am stuck with it until November 2019.  Take your $$ elsewhere for a better vehicle. You'll thank me later.

name: Raan Kway Teow
context: Time: night; Season: spring; Temperature: cold; Weather: fog
summary: Service options: Takeout THAILAND 🇹🇭 Eat the World NYC review: If you plug "raan" (ร้าน) into Google Translate, it spits out "store" in English. If you speak a little more in depth to a Thai person, they might include the word business and mention that it can naturally mean other things depending on what kind of business you are talking about. In this case, that word would trend towards restaurant, but somehow there is an enjoyable simplicity to store or business when followed by "kway teow" (ก๋วยเตี๋ยว), or noodles. At its core, this brand new Roosevelt Avenue Thai restaurant is in the noodle business.  Before the restaurant gets noticed by a wider audience, for now it is a simple star of the Thai community, all coming to check it out from listings in Thai Facebook groups and word of mouth. On a recent visit, all ages of Thai folks were coming in to see how it stacked against other neighborhood favorites. A table of four 20-somethings laughed throughout their meal, a 30-something couple quietly savored theirs, and even an elderly couple ambled in and seemed to be enjoying themselves, striking up conversations with the tables close to them.  I am naturally drawn to bowls of kway teow pork tom yum (ก๋วยเตี๋ยวต้มยำหมู, $11), a hot and spicy poem for your mouth. The version here is no let down, a symphony of different flavors all living together and never missing a note. It starts well past medium, but feel free to add more of those homemade dried chillies if desired, and plenty of the vinegar spiked with green peppers for more sourness.

context: Time: night; Season: summer; Temperature: hot; Weather: hailstorm
summary: Amenities: Good for kids The name seems to be a bit misleading: the Mount Misery trail starts here and it is the way to Oregon Butte. The road in is not bad, manageable by most cars if you pay attention. There is no water here but there is a spring up the trail a couple of miles. There are a few picnic tables, an outhouse, and areas for horses. There are some nice views and a couple of places where you could pitch a tent. Be forewarned: there are squirrels everywhere and as cute as they are they are mischievous. My camp also welcomed deer and hares. It was a pleasant evening diversion after a long car ride. From here set off to Oregon Butte and some incredible views. Be sure to say hello to Julie at the lookout.

You start near the river meandering through dense mossy forest and going over rocky creek beds. There are a few amazing spots hiking right along side of the river that rolls by you with its beautiful blue water. After a while you start to make your way uphill to Lunch Rock, an amazing spot to rest, take some pictures, and have a snack. After this you get to keep make your way up to to the next viewpoint. After this point you start to level out a bit and come along the beginning of the burn and the possibility of a lot more trees.  The trail here has a peaceful serene feeling to it where you are surrounded by trees and rock and you cant hear the river anymore. It is a great hike. Soon you start to head downhill again, where I believe you would come across 5 mile camp, but I ran into a lot of fallen trees that became to hard to climb over and under where I had to turn around and call it quits for the day.  This is definitely a hike I want to try again, maybe later in the season. But really was worth every step of my day.

name: United States Postal Service
context: Time: morning; Season: spring; Temperature: warm; Weather: partly cloudy
summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance Wow. I can not believe I pay these people to handle my belongings. I stood in line today for 25 minutes to pick up a package. The time spent there wasn't the problem at all. Watching the interactions between the staff and the customers is what makes me give one star.  One man came in to mail 3 packages. There is a small counter to the right of the service desk where people put packages that are ready to ship. The man set his 3 packages on the desk, which was already piled up, and walked away. The tall male bald man with glasses who worked there stopped what he was doing, walked over to the counter shaking his head and (not kidding) grabbed each package on the counter and threw them one by one into the rolling bin. One stack was high, so he pulled the entire stack over so the packages all just toppled into the bin and all over the floor. He then picked them up off the floor and stuffed them into the bin.. HARD. He looked me right in my eyes and shook his head as if I had too just seen the audacity of this customer to come and stack a box on top of an already full desk. I could not believe what I was seeing. Right then, the lady in front of me got called up to the counter by the woman staff member with the glasses and black hair in a ponytail. She had some garments in her hand and said she needed to mail them back to the person who had originally sent them so they could be altered to fit. The staff lady was nice and smiled, but when she was asked what the cheapest way to do that would be, said "Do you have tape for that?".... She then went on to explain that the customer could just mail it back in the original packaging she had with her but she would need to tape the top of the package back together. The customer was happy that she wouldn't have to purchase a box until she realized she would have to anyway because (again, not kidding) the lady would NOT let her use the tape sitting behind the counter. The used tape roll on the ladies desk.. Nope. I felt so embarassed for the poor woman who was trying to be so patient and just spent the last 25 minutes in line and just desperately trying to get her package mailed. The staff lady directed her to the boxes and pointed out the one she thought would fit the garments. The customer filled the box and asked again what the cheapest way to mail the box would be.. "Standard Delivery". The customer said that was perfect and that would be the way she would like it shipped please, and started to get her wallet out. "That is a first class box. You need a different box to ship Standard." ....omg. The woman asks where the other boxes are. "Over there, but we don't have any more right now. And you would need tape anyway to close it. You didn't bring your tape?"  ....I got called up next, got my package, and left. Neatest thing is, I can not decide to never give them my business again because this is my local Post Office where I get my packages. I am just disgusted.

name: IMAXShift
context: Time: evening; Season: spring; Temperature: warm; Weather: mostly clear
summary: I'm always willing to give new fitness boutiques a shot, and IMAXShift is worth a try. If you enjoy spin, I'm not quite sure how this will compare for you. It wants to hit the "experience" factor that competitors like SoulCycle talk so much about, but it also uses meters like Flywheel (the readouts show you your speed and power, etc.).  I couldn't help feeling that because of this middle area, IMAXShift couldn't fully deliver on either end. In most spin classes, you can lose yourself in the music and follow your instructor. Or you can focus fully on your own output. The main feature — the giant screen — seems to distract from both. The music didn't feel loud enough, but maybe it was just because I was distracted by the visuals. I wanted to get energy from my instructor, but kept dashing between her and the screen (instructors are off to the side here, so they don't block the screen).  Another quirky thing about the screen — there's this funny feeling as if you're in an episode of Black Mirror.  Overall, IMAXShift does a great job in terms of service, presentation, and cleanliness. The employees I interacted with were friendly and the facilities feel new and spacious. It's just that the differentiator (the screen) isn't enough to get me out here as a regular member.

summary: Service options: Online care; Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible elevator, Wheelchair accessible entrance, Wheelchair accessible restroom; Amenities: Restroom; Planning: Appointments recommended I have known since last july that something wasnt right with me physically and/or neurologically. Well in dec of 2020,because of the caring and attentive drs and neurologists that all are on the Peace Health Hospital  roster,a diagnosis was found,and not a moment too soon. Dr Modha will b doing surgery on my spine friday morning and its a procedure that is probably gonna save my life and preserve,if not,enhance my quality of life. This review will cover two points of contention and the final response from the owner. I ordered new eyeglasses at their retail cost around $1,500 last December and it took a month to receive. When I tried them on I immediately noticed a blemish on the lens. They had to be replaced. For my troubles the company gave me a half-price discount on my next pair of eyeglasses. I used the credit to replace the lenses again as I actually wanted Transitions. Also, when he marked up the glasses for Progressive lenses it was all wrong and I had trouble seeing out of them. I received the replacement lenses just as the Pandemic lockdown started so they were mailed to me. Upon trying them on and wearing for awhile I noticed that somehow they didn't apply the Transition lenses! The one thing I specifically wanted and they got it wrong again. I was upset as yet again they got my eyeglasses wrong. I asked and received a refund and was told that I could come back after the lockdown and they would fix them again. I hesitated but went back for a third time. Upon asking for payment I asked to pay upon receipt due to the past experiences. The optometrist said he understood but would need to ask the owner. The owners response was to essentially tell me to go to go to hell as he refused to do the work. They told me to either pick up my eyeglasses or have them mailed. In conclusion, the company screwed up three times. First with the lens blemish and taking a month to complete the order. Second they didn't get the Progressive lenses correct and third they didn't get the Transition lenses then refused to fix. They made it right once then decidedly slammed the door when attempting to get the Transition lenses. I ended up going to another store where I just bought an entire new pair of eyeglasses. Not one problem and I had them in one week.

I'm very satisfied and can now truly consider all my future projects with confidence.   Mike you are amazing!  And such a hardworking crew in the middle of winter- we were very impressed.  At one point even one of the Woodfords stopped by to inspect and approve Mike's  plan for one of the unexpected challenges that arose and of course that made me feel like the whole company cares about my little house.   Hoping I never have another problem like this one again but if I did, I'd use Woodford Brothers for sure. I highly recommend them.

Every item we tried was amazing. Intimately lit and cozy.  When you arrive, you get a variety of bread slices and olive oil-soaked green peppers and carrots.  For starters we tried the meatballs, stuffed red pepper and pecorino kale salad. The meatballs ($10 for 3) were served with ample sauce and on top of a juicy slice of bread. The stuffed red pepper had farro and cheese that had been broiled. The salad was my favorite - lightly dressed and creamy with a hint of pepper and crunchy croutons.  For entrees we tried two: the polenta with gorgonzola sauce and sweet Italian sausage. This dish was gluten free and yet so creamy, flavorful and filling. I had th spaghetti Bolognese (beef). The noodles were cooked perfectly and the sauce was meaty - but avoided the common pitfalls of being too chewy (fatty) or too salty.  Lastly we shared a flourless chocolate cake. The whipped cream was so good - tasted homemade and wasn't too sweet. The cake itself was also medium-sweet which I love.  Our service was amazing and the food was 5 stars. Will definitely be returning.

name: The Cardinal
context: Time: evening; Season: winter; Temperature: cold; Weather: freezing fog
summary: Fried chicken is the draw at this casual East Village Southern eatery with a down-home feel. Service options: Delivery While I am no Southern comfort food expert, I take my fried birds seriously. Deep fried food is profoundly rooted in Taiwanese cuisine, with which I grew up. You could see deep fried chicken among all night food markets and restaurants alike. Therefore, I was delighted to find out The Cardinal is a new addition to East Village, which is saturated with Asian and Italian restaurants.  I came with my husband and another couple, who were also eager to taste some American food after spending a month in Asia, eating not much butter, grease or meat in general. The decor is simple yet cozy. Exposed brick walls with whitewashed paint are decorated with antique cabinet and old books on shelves. There are few tables on the main floor and more in the basement. The vibe is casual and welcoming and we were seated comfortably close to the kitchen and bar to see some of the behind-the-scene action.  The menu itself is light weight.  There are no more than 30 items and I identified my target easily – fried chicken with two sides. That sounds like the most logical choice, right? My husband without hesitation got the carnivore choice – BBQ platter, including 3 out of 4 choices of pulled pork, links, ribs and beef brisket. It also comes with two sides. The fried chicken was a big heap and impressed I was. There are 1 drumstick, 1 giant breast and a big  thigh. The birds are surprisingly skinless but they are crispy and crunchy on the outside and juicy and tender inside. They are delicious with their house hot sauce but I think they would be even better with some additional spices. I am just saying.My husband’s BBQ platter is somewhat disappointing. Despite a pile of meat, they appear full and dry and they taste it. The pulled pork are tender but lacks the marinate to keep them in place. The ribs look malnourished and the briskets again are missing the moisture. My friend’s deep fried pork chops look much more promising however. He was pretty happy with them.  The real winner to me is this side dish. We both got the Candied Yam and it comes with melted marshmallows on top and meshed yam with brown sugar at the bottom. It is like I am eating flan, rich, sweet and irresistible. Mac n cheese is rather rich but lacks the melted cheese to bond the macaroni together. Instead, the macaroni is somewhat hard and not bonding together like they should. Maybe this is better for my health?!  Overall, I was satisfied with my choice although my husband was let down by his entree. The Cardinal has proved to be good but it can be great. The neighborhood needs a shiny star of Southern Comfort and it is not doing justice just yet.

summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance, Wheelchair accessible restroom; Amenities: Restroom; Planning: Appointments recommended We took our Rabbit Rose in a year ago for a spinal injury. Luckily we were able to see her fracture and come up with a care plan to take care of her in way that she would have the best odds at healing. While nothing was a guarantee, the vet went over every option throughly and outlined every possible outcome. We left with medication to help her her comfortable and to protect her stomach as well as a special formula food in case she wasn't eating. Every single thing that could go wrong was described in great detail as well as ways to help counteract any negative effects from her new living conditions such as urine scald and how to manually relieve her bladder should she stop going on her own. A defined set of symptoms that should bring us back immediately. They made sure we were very well informed. They were kind and compassionate. We had follow ups and continued to see improvement. We are 1 year out from her spinal injury and Rose is as close to normal as she can be. Most people don't even notice her slight limp when she is tired. Thank you to the vets here, the receptionist and the lab techs who helped us <3
