name: Narcissa
context: Time: evening; Season: summer; Temperature: hot; Weather: thunderstorm
summary: Inviting space in The Standard East Village turning out refined, farm-to-table New American cuisine. Service options: Takeout, Delivery; Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance; Offerings: Alcohol, Beer, Cocktails, Coffee, Hard liquor, Organic dishes, Vegetarian options, Wine; Dining options: Lunch, Dinner, Dessert; Amenities: Restroom; Atmosphere: Trending; Planning: Accepts reservations; Payments: Debit cards After hearing such good things about Narcissa from Eater, Grub Street, and Yelp, I had to try it for myself.  Chef John Fraser (chef from Dovetail) continues to impress.  We started out with 2 appetizers - Rotisserie Crisped Beets and Beef Short Ribs. I generally steer clear of vegetables for appetizers except brussel sprouts, but I'm glad I decided to go on an adventurous limb and try the beets. It was my first time eating beets and now I'm sure that it won't be the last. The beets were crispy and had great texture. The hint of horseradish went really well with the tangy, sweet beets. The short ribs are a must! The ribs were so tender it practically melts in your mouth.  For the entrees, we ordered the baby chicken, lacquered duck breast, and lamb loin. The baby chicken came in a pot with a variety of vegetables. The meat of the baby chicken was so tender, it fell off the bones easily.  The truffle broth was a nice touch. The lamb loin, cooked at the chef's choice of medium, was juicy and delicious. For $26, two chunks of lamb loin seem expensive, but again, it was so phenomenally cooked that it was worth it.  The lacquered duck breast had to be my favorite. Cooked at the chef's choice of medium, the meat was tender. There was a thin layer of duck fat between the crispy seasoned skin and the meat that made for a great combination of textures. The meat was juicy and the cranberries and cranberry sauce were a good addition to the flavors on the plate, which also included mashed butternut squash and pear. I loved how the sweet flavors of these components meshed with the rich, salty flavor of the duck breast.  Finally, we ordered the Winter Sundae dessert, a delectable combination of olive oil ice cream, lemon thyme whipped cream, cherries, and lemon curd. The olive oil ice cream on its own could be a bit overwhelming, but the tanginess of the lemon curd and lightness of the whipped cream made it a solid dessert. There was also some salt sprinkled in there that did a good job of balancing out the sweet and sour flavors.  Overall, I had a really positive experience and would definitely recommend this place. And since they take reservations, there's even more of a reason to take out that special someone or finally plan that dinner get-together with friends.

I will go back to them again and again!! The pricing estimates BTW were the lowest compared to 2 other similar and close auto repair places by almost 600.00. context: Time: evening; Season: autumn; Temperature: warm; Weather: rain shower
summary: Health & safety: Appointment required; Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance; Planning: Appointments recommended I have had the Brazilian wax before at other places, this was my first time at this establishment; I found the positioning for the procedure to be both unorthodox and uncomfortable.  My review below is on the Brazilian wax; as for the overall establishment it was spotless, friendly staff, welcoming environment.  To wax the vaginal area, other places have me lay with one leg extended, and the other leg bent, they would cover with a towel/cloth the area that they were not working on. When they finished one side they would have me switch position to work on the opposite.  At Trieva's Spa & Boutique I was made to open both legs wide like a frog, I felt unnecessarily exposed and had gotten muscle cramps. For the first time I had to help pull my skin, which I don't mind but it was a distraction from trying to relax, after all there wasn't much skin to pull tight.  What concerns me the most for other customers is the positioning to wax the bum area. Again, at other establishments they all had me lay on my side, and lift the knee of the leg I wasn't laying on up to my chest. Afterwards I would switch sides.  However, at Trieva's I was told to get on my knees. I was in a doggy style position (though this was not meant to be sexual, nor did the staff make me feel uncomfortable in that way) I still felt embarrassed, over exposed, and it hurt my lower back and neck.  If you have knee, back, shoulder, or neck problems I do not recommend getting the wax done here.  Because of the uncomfortable positioning methods I will not be scheduling here again.

Parking can be very difficult to find later in the evenings so it may be worth the extra cost to reserve a covered parking spot or even a garage if they are available.  The complex allows dogs of medium to small size and many tenants have wonderful dogs.  Some tenants pick up after their dogs while others don't.  If you find this review helpful give me a "Like".

name: Bellingham Fitness
context: Time: night; Season: summer; Temperature: warm; Weather: light rain
summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance Bellingham Fitness is the BEST! I joined Bellingham Fitness after I retired and moved to Bellingham to get in shape again and create a new social network.  I was delighted to see that the club was large, clean and professional, had everything I needed in one place, and that membership included most of the classes.  It was so different (and affordable) than other large chain fitness places I’ve investigated in the past.  I was also delighted to see that the staff was so friendly and helpful! I started with the morning yoga class, which is included in the membership, and lightly using the treadmill and bike.  After I worked out for a few weeks, I signed up for the personal training program twice a week because I realized that I needed to do more to achieve my goals.  I also realized I needed to learn to exercise correctly to get to my goals faster and safer. My personal trainer took the time to learn about my personal goals.  She also took the time to design a program that would work around a prior knee injury.  She gives me information that I never would know otherwise, and makes the program interesting and motivating.  Her expertise is making all the difference! It was not always easy to get to the gym and go through the personal training routine when I first started, but after six months I’m amazed at how my body has changed.  I have lost about 17 pounds and lost an amazing number of inches!  I work hard at the gym because the energy of working out with others is electric.  I never would work so hard at home.  Bellingham Fitness is the only way to go!

context: Time: night; Season: autumn; Temperature: warm; Weather: rain
summary: Service options: Curbside pickup; Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance Bloomer Creek is a winery where the philosophy may be getting in the way of the wine-making.  The owners (who also seem to be most of the staff there) appear to be of the hippy-dippy variety, which is perfectly fine and not meant to be an insult.  Their philosophy is minimal interference in the wine process, including using indigenous yeasts, organic farming, and hand harvesting, all of which is good and noble, at least in theory, and intended to duplicate Old World wine-making.  But the results do not entirely justify the evident pride.  Their Rieslings are decent but not stupendous; their other wines, including their White Horse Bordeaux blend and Gruner Veltliner, are only okay.  They were very busy the day I visited and a tad brusque.  One annoying thing that happened was that I picked a wine that I had not tasted to purchase, but when I did so one of the proprietors pointed out that I had not tasted that wine and would not permit me to do so, since none had been opened, so I was compelled to purchase something I had tasted instead.  I did not appreciate being steered away from something that might have been more interesting than their middling Gruner.  This is a small operation with a clear idea of how they want to operate, but which still seems to be trying to find its way.  Unlike Shaw, which has the same issue but considerably better wine, BC has not achieved the quality to justify the pretension.

summary: I have been flying since I was an infant and I have never in my life encountered such rude, unprofessional and incompetent people. After waiting in a line that didn't move for an hour I heard through the grapevine that the flight was cancelled but no information was given as to why.  When we get to the counter the lady knows nothing and puts us on a flight July 18 @ 1PM.  At 10AM on July 18 that flight is cancelled and they push to July 19 @ 3AM.  At this point we are irate.  They told us the July 17 flight never left Casablanca, meanwhile a friend of mine was on that flight and it arrived in NY.  On July 18 a flight went out but they said only the people booked on that flight could go and if you wanted to pay $1000 to upgrade your seat you could go in business or first class.  The police were called because statements like that really put people in a furor.  The 3AM flight has now been pushed to July 19 @ 11am.  My cousins wedding is on July 19 and I will likely miss that wedding along with 3 days of hotels I had booked in Fez.  Everyone has no information and has been wholly unaccommodating in trying to book us on a sister airline or getting us to a different city.  I will never ever fly this airline again and I hope to be fully reimbursed for my time and inconvenience.  I will report them to the BBB until they cover all the financial loss and emotional strain this has put on me and my family who had booked travel arrangements and events upon our arrival in Morocco.  This airline needs to be shut down and disbanded, it is an absolute disgrace and I wouldn't be surprised if it led to airport violence.  If it was possible to leave negative stars this is like -10, absolutely horrible!

name: Mount Teneriffe Trailhead
context: Time: afternoon; Season: summer; Temperature: warm; Weather: thunderstorm
summary: Amenities: Good for kids I had to walk a mile from the parking lot to the trailhead which divides into two.. I took the trail to Teneriffe falls, which is not very difficult it gradually inclines. The other one next to it is the easy but longer trail to the summit. The falls are pretty, I think its a couple of miles or more hike, not sure....After the falls the real challenge begins. You have to find your way up... trail is not very clear and VERY steep. Had to use my hands to climb at few places. There is a good chance of getting lost. This trail made mail box's old trail look easy. Summit itself is rocky, view is breathtaking. On the way back I lost my way  and got to the other trail which is much longer but not very steep at all. I think it is at least 7 miles. I went with my friend on a weekday and felt like we were  the only ones there. Probably there are more people on the weekends. Hiking poles are a must if you are going the way I went. You will find lots of rocks and lots of roots and everything in between. There are no markers to show you the way. For moderate level hikers, it's definitely a tough day hike.

context: Time: morning; Season: autumn; Temperature: cold; Weather: light drizzle
summary: Classic French bistro dishes in a smart, compact storefront space with sidewalk tables. Service options: Outdoor seating, Curbside pickup, Takeout, Dine-in, Delivery; Health & safety: Mask required, Staff wear masks, Staff required to disinfect surfaces between visits; Highlights: Great coffee, Great dessert; Popular for: Lunch, Dinner, Solo dining; Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance; Offerings: Alcohol, Beer, Cocktails, Coffee, Comfort food, Hard liquor, Kids' menu, Vegetarian options, Wine; Dining options: Lunch, Dinner, Catering, Dessert, Seating; Amenities: Bar onsite, Good for kids, High chairs, Restroom, Wi-Fi; Atmosphere: Casual, Cozy, Romantic, Upscale; Crowd: Family-friendly, Groups; Planning: Dinner reservations recommended, Accepts reservations; Payments: Debit cards, Credit cards Today my wife and I took my mother-in-law who is visiting from out of town to this restaurant. We had been here many times and always had perfect five-star meals. Today for some reason everything was awful from beginning to end. First, the cheese on top of the bowl of French onion soup was very much "burnt" which made the entire soup bitter with a burnt taste and inedible. We waited for the main dishes to come before we complained to the waiter about the onion soup. He offered to bring us another onion soup or something different, and we decided we should be okay with our main dishes. My mother-in-law had the hanger steak. The meat was really tough for its type and not juicy even though it was medium rare. I had the regular loin steak and it wasn't as good as I had it before - the steak quality was just really awful today for some reason, perhaps not fresh. My wife had the roasted duck. The duck was dry and rubbery and didn't taste fresh. She spoke up to our waiter about all three main dishes and the waiter had the manager come by. The manager asked my wife about her dish and listened to her complaint, but he was defensive noting that no other customers had complained about the duck today. She asked if there had been a recent change in the main chef, and was told that the same chef has been with the restaurant for 18 years. We thought this is weird given the inconsistent taste and food quality compared to our last visit. He was nice enough to offer my wife something different. My mother-in-law and I held our tongues and decided not to complain to him about our dishes because of his defensiveness. My wife decided to give the lamb a try but it was a great disappointment. The lamb was tough (and nearly tasteless) even though it was cooked medium rare. It tasted like it was cooked some time ago and was re-heated in the microwave right before being served at our table. The manager came by to check in with her, and offered something different after she described the toughness to him. She explained that she didn't want to try something different any more. My mother-in-law and I quickly wrapped up eating while my wife waited with an empty stomach and kept drinking water, so that we could get the check, pay, leave and get food for my wife from somewhere else. Overall we were really disappointed with our experience. Everything was five-star when my wife and I came many times before today over the past four years. We took my mother-in-law here to experience great French cuisine and it didn't happen today. Maybe the main chef was off today or something. To be honest, everything just tasted like they were prepared by an inexperienced cook today. Hopefully it was just an off day, because we had really liked this restaurant in the past...

context: Time: evening; Season: autumn; Temperature: cold; Weather: light drizzle
summary: Service options: In-store shopping; Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance; Offerings: Car wash, Oil change, Repair services; Payments: NFC mobile payments We never expected to walk out of Kia with the brand new Sorento we were dreaming of. Marvin Spencer gave us the deal of a lifetime. He was professional and courteous to us the entire time, even though we looked pretty rough around the edges and our one and a half year old daughter was being a holy terror for much of the time we were there. He listened to every concern we brought up and found a solution. When we had to hangout in the play room(which is such a blessing when you have a little with you) he came to us to discuss things. Being a Sunday it was impossible to get ahold of our insurance or current leaseholder over the phone. Marvin was patient and understanding while we worked around the inability to talk to an actual person. He worked miracles to get us into our Sorento. Once we were comfortable with our deal we met Andrew in finance. This man is our hero. We went back to sign paperwork and he thoroughly explained everything we were signing. Again as it was Sunday he had an approval for us but it had a high interest rate and was hoping to negotiate it down come Monday when he could talk to someone in person. He was upfront in the costs of everything and managed our expectations as to what a monthly payment would look like. On monday we received a call from him telling us he had good news and needed to get us in to sign the finalized paperwork. This man not only got our interest into single digits, but lowered our payment $40 and got us a bumper to bumper warranty too! I cannot believe the lengths he must have went to, but I appreciate him so much for his efforts.  Our experienced at this dealership was everything one would hope for. They were all kind, courteous, and upfront. Not a single person complained or seemed annoyed by our daughter, but on the contrary interacted with her as if we were friends. I cannot sing the praises for this business loud enough to do them justice.

Cool Fireplace, large sized bar, with a nicely sized restaurant, walking in, you feel the place is spacious, if you get a booth; it suddenly becomes intimate and private, the dichotomy is pretty cool.  I guess a restaurant should help you focus on the person in front of you, and it probably helps that there was a beautiful person sitting across from me.  To the Food!  I had an oven roasted chicken, served with potatoes and a nice wine reduction as the sauce.  When you oven roast chicken, there is a small window for perfection, and a large window for not so much; here, they got it just a tad over what I would have liked it, mind you, it was cooked through, I think perhaps, just a little but over, still tasty, since I did finish it. I have eaten here a few other times, the seafood plates are pretty good also, I like my food perhaps on the verge of well cooked, sometimes, maybe a little less so.  One of the main reasons I come here, is they have one of my favorite wines, Erath Pinot Noir.  A good glass of wine makes the world go round, and I have always said, a good restaurant should leave you more engrossed in the conversation, and focused on the person sitting across, and this place does that.  Here's the deal, I love this place for the ambience, the fireplace is amazing, and in Bellevue, the scene is better, and this is one place that I would recommend, if you need food and drinks.

summary: Amenities: Good for kids Patrick Park is located of a fairly quiet residential street. It has a small play structure with a slide, a selection of jungle jim equipment, three basketball hoops and a few benches. At the other end of a large field, there is a covered picnick area with tables and a barbeque grill. This park has restrooms, and (for eastern WA) plenty of large trees. It's a great place to take kids for some fresh air and the field is great for exercising pets. It is bordered on one side by a low cement embankment up to the street and on the other by a short hill down to the fenced canal, this whith the park's open layout, makes it easy to keep eyes on children or pets. This park is also a great place for some quite time because it is unusual to see more than a handful of people here. Whether you are babysitting, have children of your own or need to exercise a pet, Patrick Park is a great choice for some fresh outdoor air.

name: Verizon Authorized Retailer - Victra
context: Time: night; Season: autumn; Temperature: warm; Weather: partly cloudy
summary: Service options: Curbside pickup, In-store pickup, In-store shopping, Delivery; Health & safety: Mask required, Staff wear masks, Staff required to disinfect surfaces between visits; Highlights: LGBTQ friendly; Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance, Wheelchair accessible parking lot; Amenities: Wi-Fi; Payments: Debit cards, NFC mobile payments, Credit cards I did not personally have a good experience at this store. I decided to stop in on Black Friday thinking there would be some deals for the Pixel 3, so I asked specifically about that. The person I spoke to did not disclose a $200 discount when paying for 24 months (it worked out to $25/mo instead of the $35/mo I was quoted) and only informed me about a car GPS system you could get for free with the phone. I asked directly about my time frame for returning the phone if I didn't like it and what would be refunded if I did. He told me there was a $35 restocking fee. He did not mention that the set up fee wasn't refundable, or the screen protector, though I assumed the latter wouldn't be. I did not think to ask about the screen protector price because I've never seen one that cost $60 before, which is what he chose for me. There were no visible stickers anywhere to indicate the price either. When I decided to return the phone, because Google Fi was offering a better deal for the Pixel 3, I ended up being out about $130 instead of the $35 restocking fee I was expecting and maybe $40 for the protector. Now I know better. I understand why some items might not be refundable, but I do expect to be told all of those things when I ask directly. It's been 3 years since I got a new phone and things change over time - like the fact that you do actually get a new SIM card and that your old one won't necessarily work in the new device. I had to come back to the store to figure out why my new phone wasn't working. I'm glad Verizon ditched this old rules about SIM cards, but at least err on the side of telling everyone when they come in to renew.  I'm still leaving Verizon because I don't like how their family plans work. They're not exclusively being used by parents with underage children anymore, and they should evolve to accommodate adults who might live hundreds of miles apart or more. Multiple emails for account authentication would be great, so I don't have to ask my mother for a verification code on my behalf.  Management did reach out and they offered to refund he set up fee and give me $10 towards the screen protector, which I greatly appreciate. I don't want anything for free, just to be properly informed when purchasing.  My typical advice is to ask more questions, but that doesn't help when the answers are incomplete or misinformed. Mistakes happen. I'd say ask the same questions of multiple stores and/or of Verizon customer service. That way you can at least be aware of inconsistencies and hopefully get at the right answers from there.

context: Time: afternoon; Season: spring; Temperature: warm; Weather: rain shower
summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance; Amenities: Restroom; Planning: Appointments recommended I was referred my Dentist for a possible grafting of my gums.  I called and made an appointment and they asked if I had dental insurance.  I gave them the plan codes/numbers and they said they will have to look into if they accept that insurance.  The office called me back and said they did accept the insurance so I made the appointment for the consultation.  After the consultation told me that the business manager would be in to discuss the next steps.  She came in and told me that the procedure would be over $6000.00.  I asked how much was covered by insurance and she said it will not be covered.  I asked why not and she said it is considered "cosmetic".  I asked why wasn't I told this when I made the appointment.  She had no answer.  So when I went to check out I had a bill for over $300.00 for consultation.  I said why is that so much.  I was to told it was about $140.00 and she said we had to take x-rays.  I said why is that not covered  and she said because you just had them done at your dentist.  I said why didn't you use those x-rays and I was told they were not the same type.  Once again why was I not informed of this cost and again no answer.  I know that it is partly my fault that I did not ask more questions about insurance coverage but, I made the assumptions that when I was told that they accepted my insurance that some would be covered.  They knew from the very start that even though they accept my insurance non of the cost of my consultation/treatment would not be covered.  And to top it off they charged me for x-rays they will never use.

context: Time: night; Season: summer; Temperature: hot; Weather: thunderstorm
summary: Planning: Appointments recommended Booked a Couple's Romantic Rendezvous Package which consisted of a 90 min Deep Tissue Massage in a Couples Room and 40 minute Sauna exclusive for us during the first Saturday of the month. We were probably the first customers and we were welcomed warmly by the owner of the business and we were attended to right away and led to our room. I wish I could remember the name of my masseuse (and I typically always ask and remember! 😩) because she was that good! Well to be fair, my husband also said that he had a good massage. Our room was really relaxing, and at the right temperature too considering there was a heatwave that weekend. The music was also just at the right volume, contributing to the overall tranquility. I love that they both showed us the timer prior to starting and did set it for 90 mins. Considering we get a massage at least a month, this was one of the best that we've had. I usually dread the pain and bruising that usually comes along with it, and this surprisingly was minimal to almost none especially on the bruising part. For this alone, we're definitely planning to come back. The sauna was really nice though pretty small, but gets the job done. Obviously this would be more enjoyable during fall or winter, so keep that in mind. We were also able to shower after the sauna. My only wish and suggestion to the business would be to have shower caps, mini deodorant/antiperspirants that customers can buy, and perhaps a better selection of tea after to really complete the overall experience. By the way, I actually treated a girlfriend to a massage and facial here for her birthday before my husband and I got to finally go and she had an amazing time. Highly recommend and we'll be back! =)

context: Time: night; Season: spring; Temperature: cold; Weather: cloudy
summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance; Amenities: Good for kids This is somewhat hidden unless you live in the housing development.  There is a small parking lot beyond the gates.  Actually to the left is a paved trail that runs between a pond on the left and a stream on the right.  All flat and super easy.  It goes to another side of the development and does not loop. We saw what looked like a rat in the pond.  Odd.  Because it dived I to the water.  But there were two momma ducks and their ducklings!  So cute ☺️ Back to the parking lot.  The trail straight ahead that starts out on a bridge for a good portion of it.  When that ends it's climbs at a pretty good elevation with alot of series of 3 steps and ground. Then it levels when you come to the top by the school.  Be aware there is an ant mound to the left off trail.  The trail continues  by the school and a fence until it turns the corner and ends at another portion of the housing development.  An excellent wake you up in the morning kind of walk 😁 Enjoy!

summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance; Offerings: Oil change; Amenities: Mechanic; Planning: Appointments recommended I have to give this place 5 stars because they got me out of a very difficult situation in the most timely and effective manner possible.  I was traveling with my kid to visit colleges on Long Island. We came out to our car in the morning to drive the short distance to Hofstra University when we discovered we had a flat tire. The AAA dispatch was from Statewide, and he was a consummate professional, and also well informed about the local colleges!  He got us to the repair shop where they were able to patch the tire, but it was in bad shape and they did not recommend trying to drive back to Albany, NY with it that night. We had already had to reschedule the Hofstra appointment and also had one at Adelphi, so we drove on the patched tire to go for the appointments and returned there later to get two replacement tires that were waiting for us.  It was a most stressful experience but the people here did everything to make it less so. We were back on the road shortly after 6PM. I give this 5-star rating even though the waiting room was terrible. They had also just painted it so we had to deal with that smell, but it does look like they are trying to improve it. There was also an uninstalled TV there that I expect they will be putting up soon. For now though, if you can go somewhere else while you car is being serviced, do. But definitely feel good about having your car serviced here.

name: Indian Brook Falls
context: Time: night; Season: spring; Temperature: cold; Weather: light rain
summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance; Amenities: Good for kids A very beautiful waterfall. It is a short hike to get to it but also very rocky in some areas so watch your footing. Parking is limited to 8 spots. So if visiting on the weekend, visit early for a spot. If the lot is full, you must wait for an available spot. Do NOT park on the side or unmarked spots by the lot or your car can get towed.  Start walking on Indian Brook Road (left to the Constitution Marsh board sign). You will walk under a large, red bridge where Route 9D goes through. Very shortly you will see a small foot path next to an old, black fence. Walk in and follow the green trail markers that will lead you to the waterfall. When you cross the brook you will make a left. Continue down and watch your step. Follow the green trail markers as you follow the stream and shortly you will reach the waterfall. Be aware that the waterflow can be very heavy depending on the season and if it rained recently. Parts of the trail can be overrun by water and sometimes can be dry. You can bring extra socks just in case. Your feet might get wet. Sit and enjoy the beautiful view of Indian Brook Falls.  This waterfall has gotten a lot of exposure to the public over the past years, therefore resulting in crowding, litter, traffic at the parking lot waiting for an open parking space, etc.  But especially litter. Please do not litter and take out what you bring in. Also, swimming is not allowed although many people still do. Be aware, the ranger will kick you out if caught.

name: Gloster & Sons Auto Service, Sales & 24 HR. Towing
context: Time: evening; Season: summer; Temperature: warm; Weather: partly cloudy
summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance I completed my experience with Gloster's recently, and the following is a summary of what happened:  I needed a belt tensioner and serpentine belt installed onto my '13 BMW X3.  Gloster's charges significantly less per hour to perform work on vehicles, so I had my vehicle towed to them.  What I didn't know is that they charge a significant markup on all of their parts, and WILL NOT allow customers to bring their own parts.  In my particular situation, I had previously purchased the serpentine belt fitting my vehicle -exactly- from a nearby AutoZone, so they initially told me they would use it.  Shortly afterward, however, they told me that the belt was "too small", and I needed to pay for THEIR belt, which was almost triple the price I paid for the one from AutoZone.  My options at that point were to either pay for their parts, or pay for the diagnostic and have my car towed elsewhere, then start over.  My hands were tied, so I gave the go-ahead to perform the work.  The belt tensioner itself ranges from $100-130 anywhere you look, but they charged $230+ for theirs and wouldn't allow me to bring the one I was able to find for $125.  This, on top of the $50 for their belt.  I brought the belt I bought at AutoZone back to AutoZone, and there was nothing wrong with it whatsoever.  All in all, the work was completed; but when I went to pick up my car, the sound and feel of my car was WAY off, as if something else were wrong.  The problem ended up being a disconnected hose stemming from the air intake, which Bill and Billy both maintain that either I, or the tow truck driver must have loosened, not considering that they performed the work in the area where the hose is and they could have possibly done it, even unintentionally.  They also didn't bother to tell me that my car sounded the way it did upon start-up.  I inquired, but ultimately was left to deal with it myself.  From the beginning to end of this whole ordeal, the work that needed to be done was done.  Pros: •The work was completed. •Though reluctantly, they worked with my warranty company.  Cons: • Paid more than what I would have paid elsewhere, • Dealt with more frustration in having to debate with Bill and lil Bill about how warranty companies, money, business, and cars work, • Unable to determine sincerity of the guys here due to the shady disconnected airflow hose situation, items missing from my car, and overall condescending remarks and simply bad attitude from the owners.  In my general experience, small or local businesses offer a warm and friendly aura which acts as an invitation for customers to return, but I did not get this or anything of the sort from these guys.  I felt like they just saw me as a $ and wanted to shoo me away as soon as they could.  When I asked questions, they gave me their shortest response and hung up on me or left the room.  Highly unprofessional.  Unless it's by a stroke of sheer bad luck and I somehow get stranded here, I will NEVER return to this establishment as long as they continue their business this way.  Best of luck to any and all current and potential customers.

They keep their dogs in small glass boxes with rubber "floors" and NO bed. I don't care if your wife makes the blankets Steve, they are too small. The owner also likes to say the term "puppy mill" is not real or has not been agreed upon...  "pup·py mill noun DEROGATORY  an establishment that breeds puppies for sale, typically on an intensive basis and in conditions regarded as inhumane."  Just go through the reviews of this horrible place. The staff if untrained and uncaring, the owner is in denial, and the place is dirty and neglectful.

summary: Taiwanese cafe offering dim sum, noodle soups, dumplings & bubble tea in simple surroundings. Service options: No-contact delivery, Delivery, Takeout, Dine-in; Health & safety: Mask required; Highlights: Great tea selection; Popular for: Lunch, Dinner, Solo dining; Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance; Offerings: Comfort food, Healthy options, Quick bite, Small plates, Vegetarian options; Dining options: Dessert; Amenities: Good for kids; Atmosphere: Casual, Cozy; Crowd: College students, Groups, Tourists; Planning: Accepts reservations This restaurant is amazing! We specifically sought it out for lunch during our brief stop in Albany. Craving good Taiwanese food, after missing it for over half a year with the pandemic, we were delighted to find this gem. We dined inside, where tables for patrons were appropriately spaced six feet or more apart.  We ordered the pork soup dumplings to start. The bamboo steamer came with four for $4.95. They were probably some of the best I've had in all of New York. The skin was thin, the meat inside was flavorful and juicy, and the proportion of skin to meat was just right.  For our entrees, we ordered the beef noodle soup (how could we not? It's only Taiwan's national dish! They call it "stewed beef chuck noodle soup" here) ($10.45) and a vegetarian tofu and salted veggie noodle soup ($9.45). Both were terrific. The beef noodle soup's beef were fairly tender and very flavorful. The broth was lighter, less rich, than what I've experienced at other Taiwanese restaurants, but appreciated on a hot summer day. The tofu in the other noodle soup was cooked to perfection. Crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, rarely has tofu held center attention so well.  Service was impeccable. The restaurant was also appropriately air-conditioned inside with clean bathrooms. Definitely worth a return visit should we be back in Albany.

name: Cedars in Udistrict
context: Time: morning; Season: spring; Temperature: warm; Weather: rain
summary: Laid-back corner eatery offering both Mediterranean & Indian dishes, including tandoori options. Service options: Curbside pickup, No-contact delivery, Delivery, Takeout; Health & safety: Mask required, Temperature check required, Staff wear masks, Staff get temperature checks, Staff required to disinfect surfaces between visits; Popular for: Lunch, Dinner, Solo dining; Offerings: Comfort food, Halal food, Healthy options, Organic dishes, Quick bite, Small plates, Vegetarian options; Dining options: Lunch, Dinner, Catering, Dessert; Atmosphere: Casual; Crowd: College students, Family-friendly; Payments: Debit cards, NFC mobile payments, Credit cards If you think this is good Mediterranean, you haven't been around much. It's fast-food quality at best. We were anticipating a great meal from the reviews, but the service was awful, no one waited on us unless we physically got their attention through the whole meal. It was like they threw the food on the table and their job was done. When we did compel them to help us, it was as rushed as possible before running back to the kitchen. The food was sub-par. The dolmas (they call them "grape leaves": first bad sign) were undercooked, the rice inside was practically hard and tasted undercooked. The lettuce in our salad tasted very strange, like cleaning chemicals, and the tzatziki sauce tasted very much like ranch dressing. Hear it from a lifelong conisseur of medi food, even the pita bread "naan" was a fail, it was kind of stale, as flat as board and not even heated properly- tastes like its full of preservatives and came out of a bulk package. I literally chuckled when I first picked a piece up at how obviously crappy it was. It is not warm, delicately crispy and soft "naan," not by a long shot. It's clearly prepackaged bulk pita bread. There was no life to this bread! I think it might remain undigested in my stomach for a few months. The baba ganoush and dahl soup were edible, but we didn't feel any enthusiasm over them, just relief that they were edible, mostly. I even asked about the tzatziki sauce, which is supposed to be yogurt based with dill and cucumber. The waiter told me both times I asked that it was the right sauce and swore there was no ranch in the ingredients. If it wasn't in there intentionally, ranch dressing must have spilled into the container because it tasted distinctly like ranch. We were too overwhelmed to ask for a pass on the check for this regrettable meal, and we doubted we could even hold the waitstaff attention for long enough to be heard, so we paid and left. They did give us a free baklava, I think to belatedly make up for the complained-about sauce, but attentive and patient customer service throughout the meal would have made us much more likely to return. If you're going to serve people bad food, at least ask them how it is tasting and offer to bring them something else straight away, not as a consolation afterthought to take home with them. My dining companion and I both give Cedars Broadway circa March 2016 a solid C minus.

name: Bush Terminal Piers Park - Entrance & Parking
context: Time: night; Season: autumn; Temperature: cold; Weather: light drizzle
summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance; Amenities: Good for kids Bush Terminal Piers Park is a historic intermodal shipping, warehousing, and manufacturing complex on the Upper New York Bay waterfront in the Sunset Park neighborhood of Brooklyn, New York City. The northern portion, commonly called "Industry City" on its own, hosts commercial light manufacturing tenants across 6,000,000 square feet (560,000 m2) of space between 32nd and 41st Streets, and is operated by a private consortium. The southern portion, known as "Bush Terminal", is located between 40th and 51st Streets and is operated by the New York City Economic Development Corporation (NYCEDC) as a garment manufacturing complex.  Founded by Bush Terminal Company head Irving T. Bush in the early 1900s, Bush Terminal was the first facility of its kind in New York City and the largest multi-tenant industrial property in the United States. The warehouses were built circa 1892–1910, the railroad from 1896 to 1915, and the factory lofts between 1905 and 1925.[2] During World War I, Bush Terminal was used as a United States Navy base, though it returned to private ownership after the war. At its peak, Bush Terminal covered 200 acres (81 hectares), bounded by Gowanus Bay to the west and north, Third Avenue to the east, 27th Street to the north, and 50th Street to the south.[3]:171  The surrounding area entered a period of decline after World War II, and by the 1970s, the ports in Bush Terminal had been filled. The entire complex was rebranded as Industry City during the post-war years, though the Bush Terminal name remained in popular use. In the 1970s and 1980s, sections of Bush Terminal were demolished or converted into other uses, including a shopping mall, a federal prison, a privately operated manufacturing and commercial complex, and a garment manufacturing district operated by the NYCEDC.  Today, the Bush Terminal site collectively comprises roughly 71 acres (29 ha), including sixteen former factory buildings and eleven warehouses between built in the early 20th century. Starting in the 2010s, the complex has been undergoing renovations and expansions. A major expansion of Industry City, which would add 3,000,000 square feet (280,000 m2) of space to the complex, was announced in 2017. The section of Bush Terminal operated by the NYCEDC is also undergoing a renovation into the "Made in NY" campus, a film, TV, and fashion manufacturing complex that is set to open in 2020.

name: Dockside Apartments
context: Time: night; Season: winter; Temperature: cold; Weather: light freezing drizzle
summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance Lived here for going on 3 years and it's been nothing but bad to worse. Just want to say we live here because it is inexpensive, that is the only reason.  First week living here our neighbor was shot in what was told to us was gang violence. Our immediate neighbor had her door kicked in by police on a domestic violence call, twice.  We have had major leaks from the ceiling in our bathroom (which took them over a year to fix), when the upstairs neighbor would take a bath it would leak into ours. A leak in our kitchen that they said was coming from our dishwasher but was actually coming from the neighbor upstairs, that took months to fix but we were told to use our towels to keep the water back.  The apartment management decided to fix the rotting balconies and when the contractors came in to fix them they broke 4 of our flower pots and made a mess of our deck. We told the managers what happen and they immediately told us to take it up with the contractors and yhey would take no responsibility. Really!?  We have had rats in our outdoor storage, they did send over an exterminator who told us that we have a huge gap between the door and floor and that we needed to fill it with just a block of wood. I told the manager and she said that the rat poison would solve it and we wouldn't have to worry. Few months later we lost two suitcases from rat nesting and lots of Christmas decorations and other random stuff, no compensation was ever given.  There is absolutely no parking available here due to so many broken down cars and parked cars that don't move for months and years. There is no assigned parking. First come first serve unless you pay. Some households here have 5 or 6 cars. I get home around 10 or 11 pm and have to park in the other complex just to find a spot.  The latest thing is a broken washing machine, it's been broken for 2 weeks, unfortunately we have to constantly nag them about sending someone over here to fix it otherwise it will never get done. They've told me that they are waiting on a part, they told my wife that they have to order a new washing machine, when I asked again just a few days ago they told me that she didn't know what was going on and that matinence would be in contact with me by Monday, it is now Wednesday, still no call. They did give us keys to another apartment to use the washer there, it is winter time and it is all the way across the complex, but at least they did something I guess  If you want to save money, you can try and live here, just don't expect anything to get fixed if it breaks. I'm still living here and if anything else happens I'll keep you informed.  Update 1/4/16 Don't hang and pictures. We were told that even if we patch the holes the matinence people would charge to "touch up the paint". There is also carpet cleaning fees $70 for normal clean and more for any stains. We also were told that they send someone to sanitize on top of regular carpet cleaners that's another $110. And those are just fees not even things they need to fix or replace.  (I will leave an exit review as well)

There's a scarcity of signs showing directions from Pacific Beach town proper. You'll need to make a left at the You and I gas station/ market.  There's no sign pointing that out.  The Volunteer Camp Hosts were extremely helpful, but there was absolutely zero park employee presence at the parks check in cabin. Phone calls to that office go to voice mail and do not get answered.  We used this park to access Joe Creek to go fishing just before the afternoon incoming tide. It's easy to do, and the path is well marked. At low tide, access is mostly hard packed wet sand. Make sure you have a copy of the local tide schedule.  This is a tent and RV site.  For me, I'd like to see more trees there, but people seemed to be happy. So, if you're looking for mega sun exposure and wide open beach, this might be a good choice for you.  A few words of caution; While we were fishing Joe Creek, a group of about six horses and riders showed up down beach /closer to the river mouth. (low tide starting the upswing).  It grew into a larger group of about 12 or so. The riders took their mounts into the river, crossing back and forth just above a family with children under age 8 who were playing in the water. You could see the anger on the faces of the parents as they had to suddenly haul their children out of the water, as the horses had relieved themselves as soon as they got mid stream.  Folks, that's not being respectful of others.  Then, to make things worse, that same group, mostly late teens to early twenties, came upriver enmasse towards the 109 bridge at a trot, disregarding the signs marking private property (we were there with permission). Generally this group was not representing their lifestyle in a good way.  Don't be the horsemen.

name: NYU Dental - Urgent Care Ctr.
context: Time: night; Season: summer; Temperature: hot; Weather: thunderstorm
summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance; Planning: Appointments recommended 7th floor, Endodontics: If I could give this place -1,000 stars, I would. I have no idea how NYU continues to allow this institution to use its logo. I live in the neighborhood, and as an NYU graduate, I had high expectations for this place. First, to be seen, you have to engage in a Hunger Games scenario where you and other patients wait in the lobby until opening time, while you eye each other and attempt to stay as close as possible to the elevators; there is no ticketing system. My husband had to run up the stairs when the security gave all the ok to go upstairs, to secure one of the first spots.  2 hours later, NO patients had been called. When I was finally called, after 2  routine questions, I was told the procedure would begin. My husband, seeing a procedure would in fact begin, asked them to stop, and asked, "What's the plan exactly?" to which the dentist, who turned out to be a student, replied "An extraction". My husband went on to explain I was not there for an extraction but further evaluation. When the dentist stopped to check my electronic records, she realized he was right. I was to see the endodontist in the same clinic. We asked who was responsible for the error. To this, the student dentist replied "I just do extractions" and that it wasn't her fault that I'd ended up in that chair. When we asked to see the endodontist I had been referred to,  the supervising dentist expressed he would help us by looking into the error and seeking help from the Director.  Once at the door of the Director's office, my husband and I stayed behind- we hadn't been invited in, so we were hesitant to enter. When the Director received the dentists, she yelled, "Who are they? Close the door!" 10 minutes later, she stepped out, asked my husband to take a seat; she didn't need him to speak, she said. I intervened, and explained he was speaking on my behalf because of my tooth discomfort. She went on to add that he needed to take a seat and that she would speak to me as I was the patient, and not he. My husband replied he understood, but that she didn't need to speak down to him. It was at that moment that she seemed to register that she might be making a mistake. Turns out, the clinic serves mostly low income patients and she seemed to have gotten in the habit of speaking down to folk who might not have the time and/or energy and/or verbiage, to file a complaint. Something in my husband's tone and words softened her a bit, but she held her ground. When my husband left, she turned to me and began a pep talk on the red flags of domestic violence et. That's when it hit me. I turned to her and said, "I have something to report". The Director invited me into her office and I explained, her students had probably reported a potential domestic violence situationto cover for their near-malpractice. The Director's face turned white. She confirmed my suspicion: The student and dentist had reported my husband would not let me speak for myself and that because of this, they could not treat me.  I responded they'd made this up to cover for the fact that they'd almost earned themselves a lawsuit for malpractice. I went on to explain the actual events as they'd happened. After sharing what had actually happened, and dropping in that my husband was an MD/PhD candidate at NYU Langone, and that I was an NYU Graduate myself with experience as a Domestic Violence Counselor, her tone changed. She invited my husband into the office and gave him a half-hearted apology; the type where you explain your behavior but never say I'm sorry or admit fault . She made conversation for two hours' time while her student supposedly wrote a new referral which I didn't need, to see the endodontist. I can only guess she took her time and made sure we'd been appeased enough to not file a formal complaint. In any case, it turned out my teeth only needed a splint and time to heal. Had my husband not stopped that dentist , I would have lost my teeth and spent thousands on implants, not to mention, use a temporary prosthesis (dentures) for a while.

name: U-Haul Storage of Interbay
context: Time: night; Season: summer; Temperature: warm; Weather: light rain
summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance I had the worst move ever because of this U-Haul location.  I called the local numbers of various U-Haul locations near me looking for a 26-foot truck for a 3-day rental because when booking online, 24 hours was the longest period available and the first three I called had none available for that long.  This location was 4th on my list and the person who answered the call assured me I could have a truck that long despite her system also only allowing 24 hours.  She said just keep it three days and it wouldn't be a problem and there wouldn't be any fees.  At 10am the following day after picking up the truck, an employee from this location called asking where their truck was.  I said I was keeping it for two more days.  They told me to bring it back right away as somebody else was waiting on it.  I couldn't I said because it was full and couldn't be unloaded for hours.  They said if it wasn't back by the following morning I would be assessed huge fees and as it stood, was going to be charged a $50 dollar fee.  I explained that when I called I was assured that keeping it longer wasn't a problem.  They said the call center must have answered since they were busy and they don't have access to their scheduling system.  I worked all night to unload and load again before the next morning and couldn't finish.  I returned the truck hoping to rent something just a little smaller but they said because of my "shenanigans" the best they'd give me was a van for 24 hours.  My "shenanigans" I asked?  The call center told me I could keep it longer with no fees but the rep didn't believe me, blaming me for not speaking with an in-store employee or insinuating that I made everything up.  I took the van but after several more trips and staying up all night again I couldn't finish.  I returned the van exhausted and with no other vehicles available at any location, I grabbed a Car2Go for 48 hours to finish what I could-not sleeping a total of 88 hours.  My landlord was angry that I was two days past my lease and still had lots to move.  I finally was able to get a pickup from Enterprise and finished the next day.

Highlights: Active military discounts, Live performances; Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible elevator, Wheelchair accessible entrance, Wheelchair accessible parking lot, Wheelchair accessible restroom; Amenities: Good for kids, Restaurant, Restroom, Wi-Fi; Crowd: Family-friendly I had never been here in the five years I've lived in Tacoma. Wow! I was missing out and didn't know it. First of all, I will say that I'm a disabled woman (bad back problems), living in low-income H.U.D. housing. This is important because as a disabled person who receives E.B.T. (food stamps), I was able to buy a ticket to the museum AND get two other friends in for $2.00! Yes, you read that correctly! My friends are both able-bodied and employed but the three of us together were, for this day, anyway, considered a family. And, my two friends ARE, for all intents and purposes my family. How cool is that?  We were visiting the museum for a Washington state local authors and artists Book Fair. I wasn't sure if I would enjoy myself but I really had fun and met many Olympia and Seattle artists, producing their own graphic novels and 'zines. One of the friends I was with is a very talented illustrator in his own right and many of the artists and writers at the book fair were friends with him. I got to meet them and see their work. I even bought a few inexpensive zines. I'm kicking myself for missing out on a free workshop for creating an eight-panel zine from one regular piece of white paper. That was the workshop I really needed! LOL. Oh, well, luckily western Washington has many such workshops happening all year. We were there for that specific event so we didn't get to really explore the museum. But we definitely want to! In fact, with my EBT card, I can explore the museum now and not have to worry about the $14 admission. There are so many interesting and thought provoking exhibits that one day is not enough to completely experience all that the Washington State Historical Museum has to offer. Along with the Tacoma Art Museum, there's much to learn and enjoy about this part of the Pacific Northwest.

summary: Service options: In-store shopping, Delivery; Health & safety: Mask required; Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance; Offerings: Oil change; Amenities: Mechanic; Planning: Appointments recommended; Payments: Debit cards In 1934, Michelin introduced a tyre which, if punctured, would run on a special foam lining; a design now known as a run-flat tyre (self-supporting type). Michelin developed and patented a key innovation in tyre history, the 1946 radial tyre,and successfully exploited this technological innovation to become one of the worlds leading tyre manufacturers.[8] The radial was initially marketed as the "X" tyre.[9] It was developed with the front-wheel-drive Citroën Traction Avant and Citroën 2CV in mind. Michelin had bought the then-bankrupt Citroën in the 1930s. Because of its superiority in handling and fuel economy, use of this tyre quickly spread throughout Europe and Asia.[8] In the U.S., the outdated bias-ply tyre persisted, with market share of 87% in 1967.[8] In 1968, Michelin opened its first North American sales office, and was able to grow that market for its products rapidly; by 1989 the company had 10% market share for OEMtyres purchased by American automobile makers.[10] Also in 1968, Consumer Reports, an influential American magazine, acknowledged the superiority of the radial construction, setting off a rapid decline in Michelin's competitor technology.[11] In the U.S., the radial tyre now has a market share of 100%.[8] In addition to the private label and replacement tyre market, Michelin scored an early OEM tyre win in North America, when it received the contract for the 1970 Continental Mark III, the first American car with radial tyres fitted as standard.[12] In 1989, Michelin acquired the recently merged tyre and rubber manufacturing divisions of the American firms B.F. Goodrich Company (founded in 1870) and Uniroyal, Inc. (founded in 1892 as the United States Rubber Company).[10] Uniroyal Australia had already been bought by Bridgestone in 1980. This purchase included the Norwood, North Carolina manufacturing plant which supplied tyres to the U.S. Space Shuttle Program.[13][14] Michelin also controls 90% of Taurus Tyre in Hungary, as well as Kormoran,[15] a Polish brand. As of 1 September 2008, Michelin is again the world's largest tyre manufacturer after spending two years as number two behind Bridgestone.[16] Michelin produces tyres in France, Poland, Spain, Germany, the USA, the UK, Canada, Brazil, Thailand, Japan, Italy and several other countries. On 15 January 2010, Michelin[17] announced the closing of its Ota, Japan plant, which employs 380 workers and makes the Michelin X-Ice tyre. Production of the X-Ice will be moved to Europe, North America, and elsewhere in Asia.[18]

There's a really great selection of local cheeses with very reasonable prices, and a whole bunch of staple durable goods as well. As a general rule, I always check this place for an item before I go somewhere else. The beer selection is small, but it's all high-end local and regional craft beer that's hard to find in the West Village.  If you live near by, or just appreciate good food and supporting local business, stop in. You won't regret it.

summary: Health & safety: Appointment required; Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance I decided to write this review because I notice that some people rather spend their time writing a negative over positive one and that’s what makes a place look bad. summary: From the business: Identifies as women-led; Service options: In-store shopping; Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance; Offerings: Oil change, Repair services; Payments: Debit cards We got so far four VW's from NEMER over the years. We couldn't be happier with service and sales people. Bill the sales person, is our go to guy with personal touch and right answers for our needs. Thank you again for meeting our needs when it comes to safe and reliable cars.  What you see above is my review from few years ago. I went back to Nemer to upgrade my Jetta to a brand new one this last week... And what a mistake that was!!! I'm leaving the old positive review in place just to show how low they have went in recent years.  First, I came in on Friday afternoon to inquire about my options. I gave the sales persons my wants and my budget. We negotiated and settled on a price for a certain period of payments and I was told to come back tomorrow since it was already after the times mechanics went home and there was no one to do the inspection on my new car. I was in no rush and agreed to come back on Saturday at 4pm.  Saturday came around and even before I went back I got the call from the sales person that all is set and the only thing left is to transfer the insurance. I got there half an hour earlier to do so, no issues about that. As soon as I started working on the paperwork with the salesperson I noticed they added middle initial to my name. I don't have a middle initial. We had to redo all of the initial paperwork again. Mind you I left them with the copy of my driver license a day before , credit card application and everything that was needed to make this smooth on Saturday.  After the initial paperwork, such as registration and title were processed I went to see their finance person to close the deal we made yesterday. Even he had to redo the paperwork since he copied my address wrong and everything that was on his desk was wrong. After all of the papers and service sales shpills he vent through I was surprised to see that they added another 12 payments to the agreement we made just a day before. When I asked him about it his reply was "that's why I hate not being here when the sales are made... I had no idea they (meaning sales team) promised you such and such."  Now if this is not bait and switch by the book, I don't know what it is.  I was basically at the point where all of the information was exchanged, all of the paperwork done, my insurance transferred... Only to be told : you got 12 more payments to make on your car.  No one had a minute in the day to communicate that prior to the final paper was to be signed????  Bad hombres, bad practice and bad business.  I would never go back. If this is how they treat a loyal costumer after five cars, one can imagine how they treat walk ins.

context: Time: night; Season: autumn; Temperature: warm; Weather: heavy drizzle
summary: Amenities: Good for kids We visited on a cooler than normal, end of August day. There were really no bugs to speak of, but because of all of the standing water, I have to assume they're pretty awful in the heat of the summer. The trails were quite overgrown, often by thorny growth. But that was really only in some of the lower flat sections along the standing water.  There's a great boardwalk section that keeps you off the muddy floor.  The trails are all pretty easy, even for the toddlers in our group (3 years old). It's a small enough park that the trail maps are easy enough to follow, but the color choices are odd (like when you find yourself at a 3 way intersection where all 3 directions are blazed red). There was a Bob stroller in our group which another parent bravely pushed through the overgrowth and manhandled up the fairly rocky, root strewn, steeper slopes. So that is possible though not recommended.  Dogs are allowed off leash (if under voice control), which is great. There was a warning sign up that there were coyotes around ... So let your dogs off at your own discretion.  All in all, I think there are better parks around. Including the Whipporwill park just up the street!

I wanted to avoid being in the dealership for 6 hours like I had been an crappy dealership in Grays Harbor.  I already hesitated to go in but decided to take a chance cause I’ve been eyeing this car for awhile. Even was asked if I was interested in another model, which is annoying cause I know what kind of car I want. Every dealership that I’ve been too that wasn’t giving me a good deal does this to me. Car selling process needs to be changed. It does not suit the cusotmer at all. Even as a woman it completely discourages me from wanting to go in to any dealership. Just another same scenario for me. Again, they were really friendly, just offering a over top not an actually payment that normal people can afford now days.

name: Pep Boys
context: Time: night; Season: autumn; Temperature: cold; Weather: fog
summary: Service options: In-store pickup, In-store shopping, Delivery; Health & safety: Mask required, Staff wear masks, Staff required to disinfect surfaces between visits, Safety dividers at checkout; Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance, Wheelchair accessible parking lot; Offerings: Oil change; Amenities: Mechanic, Restroom, Wi-Fi; Planning: Quick visit; Payments: Checks, Debit cards, NFC mobile payments, Credit cards I wish I had looked at the reviews to Pep boys before I sent my family to this place today. My parents came out to the Island to visit me and their battery died. We had to have the car towed Saturday 9/26 at 6:30pm to Pep Boys. They told us that there was no way they would get to it tonight before closing at 8pm, but they would look at it first thing in the morning. Although a battery swap wouldn't take that long the garage was full and we were at the bottom of the list when they closed in an hour and a half, so we took them at their word. With no hotel and limited space, my 60 year old parents slept on the coach.  We returned today 9/27 at 9:45am. Mike the service manager and Justin another service tech seemed friendly and told us they were taking care of the car, so my father and I took a seat in their waiting room - thinking all was well. 11:15am, my father and I asked Mike if there was any update on the car. He nonchalantly told us that his mechanic put the car on the brand new lifts and popped the front driver tire. My father and I both asked why a battery change required a lift when the car and his reply was well we have to do that for all the cars. The mechanic started yelling at us that "we all make mistakes" instead of anyone saying "sorry we messed up, but we're going to take care of it." It was unbelievable. We had to ask him several times why the lift  and Mike finally said for security reasons so the cameras can see the mechanics working on the car. However, a few minutes later Mike and the mechanic told us that they put it on the lift to check out a "cranking" they heard when they went to start the car. Meanwhile his tone while explaining was condescending and elitist. To add insult to injury, the didn't have a matching tire for the truck and they had to order it from Baldwin. Mike gave us a story that the delivery trucks only make one run on Sundays and that the tire wouldn't be here until Monday. He didn't want to accommodate us nor was he apologetic for his mechanic's error that we now had to pay for. Then a few minutes later said the guy would make another run and the tire would be in around 2:30/3. He kept changing his story and what was happening. I gave him my number to call to update us and said we would be back around then to get the car. At 3pm we called Pep boys and they told us the car wasn't ready, but provided no other information. We got back to Pep boys at 3:30 and Mike ignored us. He finally acknowledged us and told us that the tire wasn't in yet. After a few minutes, he said the truck didn't come with the tire at 2:45 so he sent one of his own guys to go get it. Why didn't they tell us this at 3? Why didn't they tell us this when we first walked in? We were upset and agitated with the situation. He still did not apologize. He was defensive and aggressive. It was clear that we were stressed and upset about the situation as my parents live over an hour away and have work on Monday. He knew that he had control and was clear to show us that he had us in his grasp. The situation continued to be unresolved.  Mike threatened us and said that no one would work on the car until 6pm and it would be here another day.  He even said that we had been harassing him all day - when he only called once to check on the status and we left the store at 11:45/12 in the morning. 4:30 - still no tire and not being serviced. The mysterious "crank" in the car was never checked or resolved. Mike didn't even ring us up when the car was finally finished at 4:50! He had another person close the sale again with no apology - nothing. He was abrasive, demeaning, dishonest, and aggressive. I can't believe he is a manager and that other people on here have complained about him yet he is still working. The whole experience was a mess. I will never go there again, neither will my family, and now everyone I know here will not be going there so far I have 14 cars that used to use Pep boys that will never use them again.

context: Time: morning; Season: spring; Temperature: warm; Weather: rain
summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance; Payments: Debit cards Had a bad experience. Avoid this location.  We walked into Clark's at Southcenter Mall with the intention of buying a pair of shoes. Comfortable shoes is not an item we try to save money on. The shopkeeper insisted on fitting us with shoes that were clearly too small and kept bringing out models we were not interested in. When we let her know that we were only interested in certain models, she gave us a dirty look and made a snarky remark. She needed to throw the boxes at our feet due to a physical impairment restricting her mobility, and got aggravated, rude and slightly aggressive when we asked to try on other sizes. She took over 15 minutes to bring out the shoes from the back. Meanwhile, other customers walked in and got annoyed there was no one to help them. They asked us if we knew where the shopkeeper went. One of them mistook us for working in the store. Several of them eventually left. A second seller showed up and took over the process from the first one. She was rude and condescending. I can see how working in a shoe store might not be everyone's dream job, and I understand that everyone has better and worse days. That doesn't mean you should take it out on your customers. There's obviously an attitude issue with a number of shop keepers at this location, and the shopkeeper's inability to lift, bend, sit and walk is not being accommodated. The unfriendly and bad attitude is on the shopkeepers, but is ultimately a management shortcoming. I provided feedback to Clark's corporate office through their website and gave it a week. Since they didn't get back to me, I decided to share my experience online. We will not be buying any Clark's from this or from any other store. There are many other brands that make good shoes, and shops that provide excellent customer service. Not worth the agro.

context: Time: morning; Season: summer; Temperature: hot; Weather: heavy rain
summary: Service options: In-store pickup, Takeout, Delivery; Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance; Planning: Quick visit; Payments: Debit cards Holy cow! I almost wish for the sake of my waist I hadn't found this little gem. A couple vegan friends of mine had eloped and were coming back to work and I wanted to surprise them with something sweet... I don't even remember how I found out that this bakery had vegan options but I was pleased because this shop happened to be on my way to work!!  My bus was running a bit late so I called about 3:55 and asked if they had any vegan options today, and that I was about a block away... she told me they not only had them today BUT also everyday!!! And vegan ice cream!!! The woman (I'm guessing the owner..) waited to close until I could get there, so kind of her. I bought the whole half-dozen they had left.  The cupcakes were phenomenal!! Chocolate raspberry was the flavor... so moist and rich and decadent! There was a real raspberry compote type dressing on the top as well as fluffy chocolate frosting. I was a little worried, because I've had some very dry vegan treats before, and this is a smaller town... but I was blown away! They didn't just taste like the best vegan cupcakes I've ever had - they just flat out tasted like the best cupcakes!  Thank you so much for supporting those of us with different diets - it really means a lot to be included!  I will be coming here for all special occasion needs from now on... and hopefully not too often besides those, haha.  SUPPORT LOCAL!

Things I Dig :  1) BBQ Meat - they serve them by the lb or 1/4 lb (i.e. chicken).  I'd really just stick to the pork not so much the chicken.  The pork was tender and pretty juicy on its own but with that Saint Louis BBQ condiment that is self served by the cashier, man I'll tell ya...yum yum.  The chicken...yeah Boston Market beats this place by a mile so that's that.  2) The Bar - is amazing.  Okay maybe it is not the greatest thing you have ever seen but it is pretty damn good.  Many draft beers, many moonshine varieties, they got your hard stuff if you into that, brown liquors only I believe.  And it is poured from actual barrels.  Say whaaat?  The bartender was also cordial so there's that as well.  3) Seating - Indoor, outdoor, AND backyard.  So many options.  Outdoor is perfect for people watching or making people jealous of your food or drink as they walk by.  I mean it really is hard not to be jealous in the sweltering heat of NYC when someone else is drinking that ice cold moonshine in mason jars.  I'll let your imagination run with that one.  Indoor seating are more plentiful as it has the space of a Middle School cafeteria that is filled with communal wooden tables & seats.  Backyard, is a bit smaller than the indoor seating but more ample than the people watching outdoor seating.  And yes, the backyard is also technically outdoor.  4) Bathrooms - are clean for the most part and I feel like I'm in an very large outhouse that has plumbing.  It is definitely a different feel.  5) Service - for the most part was cordial and that can't be stressed enough.  Things I Think That They Can Improve On -  1) Sandwiches - , there are NONE.  I understand the whole slab of BBQ meat in your mouth and I can understand the need for sides, but not a single sandwich on the menu is pretty frowned upon.  Pull Pork sandwiches for instance was really what I was expecting.  Even having JUST THAT would have been enough for most people.  Sadly, that was not an option.  Unless there was a BYOB (Bring Your Own Bread) policy that I was unaware of.  Overall, I like the place a lot.  For drinks, for food, for the clientele, and if you are in the Astoria area, you need to visit this place.  Great spot to hang out, make new friends, come for 4th date or a simple couples date night, this would be my recommendation to you.  Fan.

name: United States Postal Service
context: Time: night; Season: spring; Temperature: cold; Weather: light rain
summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance 4/10/21 UPDATE-  They seem to be maintaining their good service and friendliness.  Lines move quickly and employees are generally helpful and pleasant so I'm adding an additional star.  Keep up the good work Lake City PO! UPDATE:  Well this is proof that things can change for the better and businesses, even pseudo-government ones, can listen to feedback and make positive changes.  I vowed never to go to this P.O. branch due to the rude service I received and witnessed, but I was in a rush one day and had to use this location.   The mean and rude lady wasn't there and all the employees I interacted with were helpful and pleasant....so I went back and had another good experience.  I've now been back 4-5x since my review last year and the folks behind the counter have been across the board, helpful, knowledgeable, efficient and kind. And no sign of  the supervisor from hell...maybe she got fired or reassigned to duties that don't involve interacting with the public?    I would rate the service I've experienced lately as 5 stars.....so averaging out to 3.    If this upward trend continues,  I will add more stars.   Good job turning it around, Lake City, PO! I bet it feels better to be working there too!.  Thank you!  2/1/2019 1 star~  This is the worst post office I have ever been to.  I also find it suspicious that so many other post offices have that machine at the exit that lets you rate your satisfaction by pressing one of the emojis, but this one doesn't have it. The older lady who seems to be the boss is categorically rude and does not have good customer service and is very rigid in her thinking, and unnecessarily so.   I've tolerated going here for 6 months b/c it's so close to my house but today was the last straw-- and it wasn't even me she was berating/chastising!  This poor woman had a p.o. box there that she shared with her aunt, but they don't live together.  She came to pick up her package addressed to her, but not the one for the person she shares the box with.  The worker kept arguing with her, repeating over and over that she had to take both packages.  The customer was *very* patient with her.  *I* was actually the one who lost my temper and told the worker to figure it out!  If you can't figure out how to adapt to less common occurances that come up from time to time, you're not fit for today's workplace.  I was so frustrated with how she was treating the customer,  I left and drove to another post office 12 minutes away (Bitter Lake, who were very nice and patient with both me and the customer before me).   There's so many horrendous and difficult things happening in the world today,  do we really need a simple trip to the post office to be one of them?  We each have the power to make someone's day better or worse; choose well. I will not go back to this location.
