name: Fall Creek Family Dentistry
context: Time: night; Season: autumn; Temperature: warm; Weather: heavy drizzle
summary: Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance; Planning: Appointments recommended Dr. Luis Mauleon was my dentist here growing up until I was 18. Over the years he gave me 4 metal fillings in my molars. When I was 21 one of the fillings he put in became infected and needed a root canal. I went to another dentist to get a crown put on. After x-rays the new dentist said that all the fillings Dr. Luis Mauleon put in had infections because they were done with metal, which wasn't a common filling material even when I was a kid. Dentist's are supposed to use the white filling material because it doesn't expand and contract, causing leakage and fractures in the tooth.  The new Dentist ended up crowning a different tooth than I went in for because the filling on it that Dr. Mauleon put in went way too deep, all the way to the root, leaving it exposed to potential infection, and causing it to fracture. He put the crown on but warned that it might need a root canal because it was drilled so deep originally. Because I got that crown I couldn't afford the crown on the tooth that had the root canal that I went in for. That tooth split in two because the original filling was too big and weakened the walls of the tooth, which combined with the brittleness caused by root canals meant it was going to fracture eventually. So that was pulled.  Update: the tooth that I got the crown on became severely infected in October of 2018 and had to be removed. Another tooth lost because of the initial work of Fall Creek Family Dentistry.  My sister had the same dentist, Dr. Luis Mauleon, growing up. Because of the way he did her fillings she had to have a root canal recently as well.  My mom hasn't needed a root canal for 52 years, but recently she saw a new dentist who told her that because of the way a filling Dr. Luis Mauleon did was put in, and because of the metal material used, her tooth was fracturing and needed a root canal and a cap. She wouldn't have needed that is Dr. Luis Mauleon hadn't filled her tooth improperly.  I've heard a story of someone who Dr. Luis Mauleon was operating on. He was drilling out a tooth for a filling and drilled so deep he punctured the sinus cavity above the tooth.  Our family has deep pockets in our teeth, meaning that the tops of the molars recede deeply into the teeth, this causes a little browning very deep in the pocket that can appear to be a cavity, but based on all my dentist visits after leaving Dr. Luis Mauleon these pockets have been confirmed to be fine. Not cavities. I've asked other dentists about it and they said that it was possible the original fillings were never needed, because my whole family got the fillings at the same time. We've never had cavities since then, though we don't take as good care of our teeth as we should. We haven't changed our brushing habits since we had the cavities, yet no more have grown. So I have to conclude that we most likely didn't need the fillings in the first place. It's unlikely my whole family, ranging from 5 to 35 at the time, developed cavities at the same time.  I'm surprised there isn't a class action lawsuit against this practice. The damage Dr. Luis Mauleon has done has cost me thousands of dollars, and will cost me thousands more for the bridge or implants I'll need to get for my two lost teeth. I believe he's responsible for these costs. His damage caused these problems and cost me more money than I can afford. All the teeth he never touched are fine.

name: Mavis Discount Tire
context: Time: night; Season: spring; Temperature: warm; Weather: mostly clear
summary: Service options: In-store pickup, In-store shopping, Delivery; Health & safety: Mask required, Staff wear masks; Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible restroom; Offerings: Oil change; Amenities: Gender-neutral restroom, Mechanic, Restroom, Wi-Fi; Planning: Appointments recommended; Payments: Checks, Debit cards, Credit cards My car went in to have the tires swapped from winter to summer. The appointment was at 8am, I arrived at 750 am. I proceeded to wait in the waiting area until almost 930 am while three uniformed employees conversed about the relevant musings of the previous day. They were waiting for a single employee to show up to work that was over an hour and a half late, before anyone bothered to start on my car for a simple tire swap. They then proceeded to inform me that my ball-joint was bad. I couldn't hear the rattle they described but told them to go ahead and change it anyway, because the car was beginning to age and this was not beyond the realm of possibilities. Five and a half hours later they finally finished the installation of the new ball-joint,with the aid of lots of big hammers, fire, impact tools and cursing. I drove the car home and noticed a very loud crunching sound in the exact wheel they supposedly had just worked on. Me being a helicopter mechanic in the past, took a look under the car. I found that the ball joint was installed without a spacer, and that the castellated nut was left loose and the cotter pin almost a full inch away from the head of the castellated nut. There was also a tremendous amount of grease all over the place due to the CV boot having been punctured by the mechanic that worked on the ball joint. I called them and they claimed that they could not meet with me until next Thursday because the district manager was on vacation. Next Thursday came and the district manager wasn't even called to come see the problem (so almost a week went by for no reason other than laziness and disregard for consumer safety). They then proceeded to inform me that the car had to be held for a few days until the correct part could be ordered (if the mechanic hadn't thrown the spacer out with the old part they could have just used one from the local B&M). Four more days go by and I still get a bill that showed the part being "discounted" from a 150% mark up and double the labor time. Then I get home to find that it wasn't the ball joint but a say bar end-link that was making the noise and I changed it myself in my drive way in less than a half hour. Their common procedure is to bait you with very low cost maintenance then ask to fix minor issues for hugely inflated labor rates and part markups. At the very minimum this place should be shut down and the facility sold to a reputable competitor. Absolute scam this place is. I drive a late model Subaru, a very common vehicle in this part of the country. Absolutely no excuses.

The entrance is located in the current train station, which was bright, clean, and modern, which provided a nice contrast to the old Customs house where the museum is actually located. It's not very large, but it's packed with history and is organized well. Seeing photos of what crossing the border was actually like back then was extremely powerful. To realize what people went through just to make it to this point, and that freedom was within eyesight... Only one mighty obstacle to go. I highly recommend this museum. You can almost feel the torrent of emotion that must have been as powerful as Niagara Falls itself. I found this to be a very emotional experience.

Would not recommed this place.

context: Time: morning; Season: winter; Temperature: cold; Weather: clear
summary: Polished restaurant with harbor views offering pasta, steak & seafood, plus Cajun-Creole classics. Service options: Curbside pickup, Takeout, Dine-in, Delivery; Health & safety: Mask required, Staff required to disinfect surfaces between visits; Highlights: Great coffee, Great dessert; Popular for: Lunch, Dinner, Solo dining; Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance, Wheelchair accessible seating; Offerings: Coffee, Comfort food, Healthy options, Organic dishes; Dining options: Dessert; Atmosphere: Casual, Cozy, Romantic, Upscale; Crowd: Groups, Tourists; Planning: Lunch reservations recommended, Dinner reservations recommended, Accepts reservations; Payments: NFC mobile payments We had the best experience at Gordon's. Our friends invited us and assured us that even though we are vegan (they are not) there would be options for us. We ordered the spinach pear salad without the goat cheese for starters. That was delicious and fresh. Then we told our server that we were vegan and she said that chef Gordon loves to make food to order for different dietary preferences. We said whatever he'll make we'll take it. We expected to both get the same dish of measly steamed vegetables, which is what we've gotten at other nice restaurants which said they cater to different diets. But what we got instead would rival the finest dishes at restaurants in Seattle dedicated to vegan food. We each got a different meal. Mine was a noodle stir fry with root vegetables, kimchi, brussel sprouts, all in a light coconut curry sauce. I couldn't keep track of all the delicious foods in my bowl, but the flavors all went so well together. My husband got a coconut rice dish with a Portobello mushroom steak crusted with pistachios and pomegranate seeds. My goodness. We were both blown away with our meals. Chef Gordon himself came into the dining room and made his rounds and we got to tell him how impressed we were with his vegan dishes. We will hopefully be back, and we'll tell everyone we know to check out Gordon's on Blueberry Hill on Whidbey!

name: Walgreens
context: Time: morning; Season: autumn; Temperature: warm; Weather: rain
summary: Drugstore chain with health & beauty aids, prescriptions & photo services, plus mini-mart basics. Service options: Curbside pickup, Delivery, In-store pickup, In-store shopping; Health & safety: Mask required, Staff wear masks, Staff get temperature checks, Staff required to disinfect surfaces between visits, Safety dividers at checkout; Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance, Wheelchair accessible parking lot; Offerings: Passport photos; Planning: Quick visit; Payments: Debit cards, NFC mobile payments, Credit cards I came in there in the early evening to grab some batteries for my bike light. I was wearing khaki pants, a collared shirt, and a bicycle helmet. I was in a wonderful mood, in fact, I was giggling about the Halloween decorations and having the time of my life for a good solid minute or two. Apparently, some middle aged neurotic woman was overwhelmed by the smell of cannabis coming from me, and she drummed up this huge controversy at the register. She was very loud and very sassy and very sure of herself and her moral superiority. Her voice was kinda like if you ran a cheese-grater over a chalkboard, you know, one of those, called everyone Hun and all that. I went outside to grab my money, and when I came back in, the employees were all huddled around the woman, and they were all talking about me and how horrible I had made their lives.  I brought my purchase to the register, and they continued talking about me as if I wasn't there. Finally, the original woman left, and to my amazement, the cashier was now talking, directly to me, about how the odor was causing her a headache, while the other employee who had been tailing me through the store earlier was now pacing around very vocally searching for an aerosol spray.  Okay, that's enough. Frankly... Grow up. The war on drugs is over. You lost. Cannabis is legal. While I'm not particularly pro-cannabis, I am particularly pro freedom, especially hard-fought freedoms (my father served a five year prison sentence for growing weed), and pardon my french, but placing my odor or my personal habits under public, LOUD moral scrutiny is just, well, for one thing, it's impolite. For another, it's unprofessional. But then, the bottom line is, I have a college degree. I work hard at my job, I'm kind and caring and careful. I don't feel like an adult cashier at Walgreens is in any position to tell me how to live my life, to look down her nose at me, to treat me like a nuisance or a freaking criminal. As for the smell, well, it's not like I was smoking in there. You're offended by the way I smell? Well, that's just rude. This is a stinky world. I can't be one of the more stinky customers you've helped today. No, this was a moral thing. This was not-so-subtle public ridicule. And you know what I said to her? I told her that I knew something that would help with her headache. I really did. I'm so cool!  To the women who slighted and ostracized me, I have this to say. I'm not ashamed of my behavior. I'm ashamed of your rudeness and lack of tact and professionalism. That was way out of bounds, unforgettably deplorable customer service. And not that I matter in the grand scope of things, but yeah, I'll now avoid the closest pharmacy to my house because I don't want to be henpecked by a bunch of killjoy shut-ins. Yeah, that's worth an extra few blocks of pedaling. But seriously, where are all the Christians around here???

context: Time: night; Season: autumn; Temperature: warm; Weather: partly cloudy
summary: STAY AWAY! This apartment complex is INSANELY unprofessional and poorly kept. I had bed bugs twice, multiple maintenance issues that were half "fixed" time and time again (tiles coming up, garbage disposal breaking, smoke alarms dying, etc.). Power always went out. They cap the heat at 69, so prepare to freeze. Everything is completely outdated. Fellow tenants are loud and disrespectful (or maybe that's because you can hear EVERYTHING through the paper thin floors and walls). Washing machines don't work. Some maintenance workers are truly nice and helpful, but I often heard the same few arguing with the landlord in the parking lot loudly (They have even gotten into physical fights with tenants). I never made a peep and always got along with the staff until the day I moved out: We had a car parked with the hazards on in front of the building for all of an hour as we were lugging heavy furniture out. This awful woman on a golf cart blazes up, SCREAMS across the parking lot that we need to move or we'll be towed. We ask nicely if we can leave it since we literally had a few boxes left. She began yelling even louder and was disgustingly rude. Mind you, people have parked their cars overnight because they're lazy and not a damn thing is said.

The table I was seated at had their air conditioning vent right above it, so every plate of food that came out became cold really easily and I don't know why but they were really blasting their a/c, so much so that I was getting pretty cold and didn't want to be there anymore.  I tried the eel kimbap, the seafood pancake, and the braised short ribs. The kimbap was smothered in eel sauce and was way too sweet but the pancake and the ribs were good but not amazing. And therein lies the reason for my negative review. Restaurants like this one put up fancy decor and good service to charge you at ridiculous prices for their food that's only just as good or oftentimes worse than cheaper places you can find in Koreatown. For example, the short ribs ("Kalbi Jim") were decent but for all its fancy plating, it lacked flavor and was definitely not worth $32. Their menu reads like a normal Korean menu; there is no creativity here like you'd find at Atoboy or Oiji.

name: Confluence Health
context: Time: night; Season: winter; Temperature: cold; Weather: clear
summary: Service options: Online care; Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible entrance; Planning: Appointments recommended I've had quite a few health troubles the last few years, running the gamut of weird bad luck specialty stuff to everyday illnesses. I don't really understand the number of 1-star reviews; in some cases I can understand that someone just had a REALLY bad experience. But in other cases, it feels like maybe folks do just miss the smaller community atmosphere of pre-Confluence. I wasn't here then so I can't speak to that.  But I can speak to the fact that it's the best & most consistent care I've received ever. I have had a TERRIBLE appointment or two, and I voiced my thoughts via survey. But a handful of bad appointments out of the 50+ good ones I've had the last 4 years with 10+ practitioners? Not bad.  I'd agree that the mental healthcare aspect could use some bolstering. I think even just a renewed focus on communication could be useful. For example, explaining that the mental health providers at Confluence have short visits & follow a more clinical protocol before someone waits months. Recommending setting an appointment and seeking out a private psychotherapist until that point. Mentioning that your PCP can likely prescribe you the psych meds you need and to try to get you in with them same or next day instead of recommending the ER. Recommending the walk in before the ER for mental health.  Also the waits can be quite long (weeks to months) to see providers about specific things. But the ability to call the provider's office and saying something is wrong can trigger them to see you sooner if warranted, & mychart is a fantastic resource for easy Q&A with your providers.  Plus, creature comforts like no paid parking, Curby for mobility-challenged folks, the willingness to do payment plans, mychart, being recognized by healthcare workers (a walk-in doc recognized me a year after I'd last seen her - amazing!) - it's nothing like the care I usually received at larger city health centers.  Maybe I've just been lucky in my experiences but for anyone nervous to try Confluence based on the reviews, I just felt I should chime in with my own positive experience.
